# Why calibrate IMUs together | OpenMVIS

URL: https://openmvis.com/why/multi-imu/

This page shows why a rig with several IMUs needs them calibrated against each other. You need nothing to run
here. Most numbers come from our published runs on VI-Rig; sections 3
and 5 add unpublished studies, marked where used.

The answer first:

- No shared clock: each IMU stamps its data on its own clock. On the running example, the T265 IMU is 7.2 ms
off the Xsens.

- No shared origin: each IMU sits at its own place on the rig, with its own rotation.

- What MVIS solves: the base IMU is the one the trajectory and the reference clock hang on; every other
IMU is an aux IMU. For each aux IMU, MVIS solves its lever (position), rotation, td and t_ga
against the base IMU.

How to turn it on: Turn on the aux spatial and temporal terms.

## The setup

- Base IMU: the IMU the trajectory and the reference clock hang on. Every other sensor is solved against it.

- Aux IMU: any other IMU on the rig.

- Lever: the position of an aux IMU in the base IMU frame.

- td: the time offset of an aux IMU’s clock to the base clock.

- t_ga: the time offset between an IMU’s gyroscope and its accelerometer.

## 1. Each IMU has its own clock offset and pose

All four cameras and all four IMUs in one solve: example run.

- Data: VI-Rig 4 IMUs + 4 cams, recording 4imus_4cams_01.

- Base IMU: the Xsens MTi; the other three are solved against it.

IMU | Rate | Lever (mm) | $\log\mathbf{R}$ (rad) | td (ms) | t_ga (ms) |
Xsens MTi (base) | 400 Hz | 0 | 0 | 0 | −0.82 ± 0.02 |
MicroStrain GX3-25 | 500 Hz | [−122.8, −45.3, −3.1] | [+2.2502, +2.1849, −0.0279] | −0.69 | +0.10 ± 0.02 |
MicroStrain GX3-35 | 100 Hz | [−82.3, −46.2, −3.5] | [+2.2304, +2.2070, −0.0192] | −2.07 | +0.01 ± 0.02 |
T265 IMU | 200 Hz | [+54.7, −107.4, −30.3] | [+1.5724, −0.0054, −0.0113] | −7.17 | −6.74 ± 0.02 |

- Frames: each lever and rotation is the aux IMU in the base IMU frame. Rotations are $\log\mathbf{R}$ in rad.

- td sign: $t_I = t_{I_j} + t_d$, with $t_I$ on the base clock and $t_{I_j}$ the aux IMU’s own stamp.

- Time: the aux IMU clocks are 0.69 to 7.17 ms off the base clock.

- t_ga: only the T265 IMU has a large gyro–accel offset; the other three read near 0. See
Why calibrate t_ga.

## 2. MVIS levers repeat several times tighter than Kalibr’s

Every recording of each dataset, from the results pages.

- Spread: how much each value moves over recordings, as the standard deviation (sd). A small spread means the
value repeats; it does not prove it is right.

- MVIS column: for the 4 IMUs + 4 cams set we use “MVIS (K-IMU)”, MVIS run with Kalibr’s IMU convention, so
the IMU terms mean the same in both tools.

- No Kalibr run: the 5 IMUs + 4 cams set has none, so its numbers are plain MVIS.

4 IMUs + 4 cams, mixed T265 left + ELP left run, T7 (T265
IMU base, Xsens aux):

Xsens vs T265 IMU | MVIS (15 recordings) | Kalibr (14 recordings) |
td | 7.240 ms (sd 0.146) | 7.260 ms (sd 0.122) |
distance to base $\lVert\mathbf{p}\rVert$ | 124.09 mm (sd 0.32) | 114.10 mm (sd 2.96) |

- td agrees: the two tools are 0.02 ms apart.

- Same offset, other side: with the Xsens as base (section 1), the T265 IMU td is −7.17 ms. With the T265
IMU as base, the Xsens td is +7.24 ms.

- Lever differs: the tools are 10 mm apart, and Kalibr’s spread is about 9× larger.

- Unequal counts: Kalibr failed on one recording.

- T8, a rough check: on the ELP pair with the same two IMUs, MVIS gives 123.94 mm, sd 0.30 over
15 recordings, and Kalibr 115.85 mm, sd 1.24 over 3 recordings from separate earlier runs.

More: VI-Rig 4 IMUs + 4 cams results.

4 IMUs + 3 cams, T6 (Xsens base, three aux IMUs, 10 recordings each):

Aux IMU | MVIS lever sd | Kalibr lever sd |
GX3-25 | 0.20 mm | 0.88 mm |
GX3-35 | 0.19 mm | 0.86 mm |
T265 IMU | 0.19 mm | 1.42 mm |

More: VI-Rig 4 IMUs + 3 cams results.

5 IMUs + 4 cams (Xsens base, two T265 units, 7 recordings, MVIS only):

| td (ms) | distance to base $\lVert\mathbf{p}\rVert$ (mm) |
T265 A IMU | −7.170 (sd 0.115) | 180.77 (sd 0.40) |
T265 B IMU | −7.259 (sd 0.120) | 188.60 (sd 0.41) |

- Two units, same offset: both T265 IMUs sit about 7.2 ms off the Xsens.

- Nothing to compare: this set has no Kalibr run. More:
VI-Rig 5 IMUs + 4 cams results.

## 3. The aux IMU lever does not depend on the cameras

- Test: T7 and T8 solve the same two IMUs (T265 IMU base, Xsens aux) on the same 15 recordings. Only the
cameras differ: T7 uses T265 left + ELP left, T8 the ELP pair.

- Results medians: the Xsens distance to base is 124.09 mm in T7 and 123.94 mm in T8.

- Per-recording gap: in an unpublished study, the gap between the two runs’ Xsens levers was 0.11 mm.

- What it means: the aux IMU lever comes from the IMUs, not from which cameras are in the solve.

## 4. Several IMUs constrain each other

Several IMUs see the same motion. That redundancy constrains what one IMU leaves weak:

- Time offsets: every IMU must agree on when each motion happened.

- IMU intrinsics: scale, misalignment and similar sensor errors, Dw and Da.

- A meaningful check: a wrong calibration usually cannot satisfy every IMU at once. This makes the
round-trip check useful on these rigs.

## 5. Slow IMUs bias levers on short windows

- Twin: a noise-free simulated copy of the 4 IMUs + 3 cams rig with known truth and true t_ga = 0.
Unpublished.

- Measured: lever error at aux factor intervals 1 / 2 / 3.

IMU rate | Interval 1 | Interval 2 | Interval 3 |
100 Hz | 2.94 mm | 1.47 mm | 0.63 mm |
200 Hz | 0.56 mm | 0.30 mm | 0.17 mm |
500 Hz | 0.11 mm | 0.05 mm | 0.05 mm |

- Why: at 100 Hz an aux factor at interval 1 holds only about 3 samples.

- Default: MVIS upsamples an IMU slower than 200 Hz before it integrates it
(solve.imu_min_rate_hz: 200, solve.imu_upsample_method: cubic).

- Upsampling helps: in the same twin, cubic upsampling of the 100 Hz IMU gave 0.80 / 0.52 / 0.12 mm.

- The knob: solve.aux_imu_stride sets one aux IMU factor per this many base intervals. The default is 3.

- Levers move with it: keep the default unless you have a reason, and compare runs only at the same value.

Conclusion:

- Calibrate every IMU: each aux IMU has its own clock offset and pose, and MVIS solves both in one graph.

- The levers repeat: MVIS levers repeat more tightly than Kalibr’s and do not depend on the cameras.

- Mind slow IMUs: keep the upsampling and stride defaults, and compare runs only at the same stride.

## Limits

- Slow IMUs: on short windows they bias the lever; the twin numbers above are unpublished.
- Camera-only and camera–IMU readouts differ: MVIS reads the ELP readout as 16.6 ms with the IMU and 14.6 ms
camera-only. We have not found the cause yet. See
Rolling-shutter calibration, section 4.
- Pick the base with care: the base IMU carries the trajectory and the reference clock. Its errors
reach every other sensor.
- Repeatable is not right: spread over recordings shows precision. There is no reference lever for
these rigs.
- Who ran it: we ran every solve.

## Data

- Recordings: the VI-Rig datasets on the Hub,
calibench-vi/datasets.

- Published runs: the results pages and the example run linked in each section. The 4 IMUs + 4 cams and
4 IMUs + 3 cams rows are batch 2026-11-10a; the 5 IMUs + 4 cams rows are batch 2026-11-02.

- Camera-set gap study: MVIS main of 2026-11-02; unpublished.

- Slow-IMU twin: noise-free twin; unpublished.

- Citation: please cite the VI-Rig dataset and MVIS.

## Related

- Multi-IMU spatial-temporal calibration: the config, step by step

- Why calibrate t_ga

- Why calibrate cameras together

- Auxiliary IMU factor

Who ran it: we ran every tool ourselves, including Kalibr and Basalt, with its documented defaults unless a family's notes say otherwise.
No totals: nothing is added up across cells, families or datasets, and rows are never ordered by a value.

◆ counts are the rows where two tools' medians differ by more than the larger of their spreads,
counted by the same code as the parameter tables. They mark disagreement, not who is right. On camera + IMU
families the MVIS of these pairs is its run with Kalibr's IMU model (K), so the IMU terms
mean the same thing in both tools.

How to read a cell

- Each repeatability cell is one family and one group of parameters, compared on the recordings every compared tool ran. Its shape names the tool whose estimates scatter least; two shapes are a tie between them, both ahead of the third.
- ≈ is a tie: the gap is within chance or under 20 %. The hatched box means too few shared recordings to decide (fewer than 6). ○ means a tool received the values as input, so there is nothing to compare; – means the tools’ models differ there.
- Point at a cell for its sentence; click it for its numbers on the results page. Nothing is counted per tool across cells.

Run dates and data settings

- 2026-11-08: MVIS and Kalibr on T6 and T11, and Basalt on T11, were re-run with IMU noise measured at rest (white-noise density × 2.5, the same values for every tool; bias walks at the defaults).
- 2026-11-08: MVIS on T2 and T12 was re-run with the current MVIS code.
- 2026-11-07: Kalibr camera + IMU on T6 and T11 was re-run from its own camera calibration.
- 2026-11-07: on T3, every tool ran on the same view-filtered bags (≤ 85°).
- 2026-11-04: Kalibr on T1 bag 09 was re-run.
- 2026-11-02: Kalibr on T7 was re-run.
- 2026-10-22 or earlier: all other Kalibr and Basalt runs.
- T6c: the MVIS values come from camera-only runs.
Data settings still differ from MVIS on T6, T7 and T8.

## About these results

How each cell is decided: see Repeatability verdicts on Methodology.

◆ differences between tools
The ◆ columns count, per tool pair, the parameter rows where the tools’ medians differ. No tool is the reference. The results pages chart each tool’s values per parameter; they do not list the ◆ rows.

- Disagreement: two tools disagree where their medians differ by more than either tool’s scatter.

- ◆ marks disagreement, not an error in either tool.

- ‡ on a time offset: MVIS splits the gyro (td) and accel (td + t_ga) timelines, so Basalt − Kalibr is the like-for-like check there. Here td is the camera–IMU time offset, and t_ga is the time offset between the gyroscope and accelerometer channels.

Family numbers
Each family is one test in the MVIS regression suite. On 2026-11-02 the numbers changed so the VI-Rig datasets come first. Older material uses the old numbers.

New | Old |
T1 | T3 |
T2 | T4 |
T3 | T1 |

# Methodology | OpenMVIS

URL: https://openmvis.com/benchmark/methodology/

Use this page to read the Leaderboard and the results pages: what their numbers mean and how we make them.
The metric definitions are shared with Evaluation & metrics.
So a local run and a published entry measure the same thing.

## What the pages show

- Three tools: MVIS, Kalibr and Basalt each calibrate the recordings of a rig.

- The Leaderboard puts every dataset and family on one screen, one row per family
(one test in the MVIS regression suite). Filters pick the mode (camera only, camera + IMU) and the shutter.
Each row shows:

- Solved: how many of the family’s recordings each tool solved.

- Repeatability cells: one per group of parameters (f + pp, Dist, Base, Readout, td, Lever, Gyro, Accel).
See Repeatability verdicts.

- ◆ columns: per tool pair, how many parameter rows differ by more than the spread. See Differences.

- Each results page (for example VI-Rig 4 IMUs + 3 cams) holds one dataset:

- Header: chips for the data and its cameras, the batch and results commit, and links to the dataset page,
the Device wiki and Hugging Face.

- Notes: a study’s reading notes, on the pages that have them.

- Per family: its title, the number of recordings and a “Read first” line.

- Coverage: each tool’s solved n of N, the reason where a tool did not run, and the record files behind the numbers.
A closed Fit fold gives the reprojection median per camera and tool: fit of each tool’s own model, not accuracy.

- Parameters by sensor: one tab per sensor, one chart per parameter, one lane per tool.

- Each lane: a parameter as median ± sd (n), across the recordings that tool solved.
sd is the standard deviation; n is the number of recordings.
The whisker runs from the lowest to the highest value, the box is median ± sd and the tick is the median.
A hollow box is an input, a hatched one another model (printed, not drawn), a dashed one no value.

- Two MVIS lanes on camera + IMU families: MVIS ran twice per recording, with its default IMU model (“MVIS”)
and with Kalibr’s IMU model (“MVIS (K-IMU)”), so the IMU terms of the second mean the same thing as Kalibr’s.

- Not on the pages: rotations (the records do not hold them yet), per-row difference tables and run configs.

- No totals: nothing is added up across cells, families or datasets, so there is no score or rank.
A single number would encode a judgement about which parameters matter.

Differences are not errors
These datasets have no metrological ground truth.
A difference shows that two tools disagree, not which one is right.
A small spread shows repeatability, not accuracy: a method can repeat the same bias on every recording.
MVIS checks accuracy separately, against known truth, in its digital-twin regression
(Regression testing).

## Differences

The ◆ columns are on the Leaderboard only. Per tool pair, they count the parameter rows where the two medians differ
by more than the larger of the two spreads, out of the rows compared.
On camera + IMU families the MVIS of each pair is its run with Kalibr’s IMU model (marked K).

A row is not compared where a difference would mislead:

- values a tool takes as input

- values shown only

- missing values

- rows where the tools’ models differ

Reprojection error isn’t compared, because it measures fit.

## Values that aren’t estimates

These are the words a results page prints beside a value, or in place of one.

Label | Meaning |
input | The tool takes this value as input, for example the intrinsics in Kalibr’s camera + IMU runs. It is printed, not compared. |
different model, not compared | The tool estimated it with a different model, so it is printed, not drawn, and not counted in the ◆ columns. |
different model, no value | The tool uses a different model here and has no value for this row. |
not in this tool's model | The tool’s model has no such parameter. |
not reported | The tool does not write this value out. |
not in one run | The tool ran with each sensor, but no single run holds both ends of the baseline. |
not run | The tool never ran with this sensor. Where a whole family was not run, its coverage line gives the reason. |
no value | The tool has no value for this row. |
3 of 15 | In Coverage: the tool solved only 3 of the family’s 15 recordings. |

## Repeatability verdicts

For each family and group of parameters, we decide a verdict in five steps:

- We take only the recordings every compared tool ran.

- For each tool, we measure the scatter (standard deviation) of each parameter across those recordings.

- We compare two tools by the median ratio of their scatters.

- A tool is marked more repeatable only if both of these hold:

- its scatter is at least 20 % smaller, and

- a gap that large would rarely appear (under 5 %, Holm-adjusted within the cell) if we swapped the two tools’ results recording by recording.

- Otherwise it is a tie: either the gap is within chance, or it is under 20 %.

Notes on the test:

- Too few recordings: with fewer than 6 shared recordings, no gap can pass this test (the smallest possible p is 2/2ⁿ). Those cells say “too few recordings”.

- Not compared: values a tool received as input, and rows where the tools’ models differ.

- Distortion coefficients trade off against each other, so their scatter can overstate differences in the lens mapping.

- Many tests: each cell is a separate 5 % test. Across the 27 tested cells of this batch, of which 14 name a tool, one or two calls may be chance. The intervals are not adjusted for multiple tests.

## Known limits

- Dates: MVIS rows and the Kalibr and Basalt runs were not all made on the same date.
Data settings differ on T6, T7 and T8.

- Recording counts: these differ per tool on some families, so a difference can mix recording sets.
Each lane prints its n, and Coverage gives n of N per tool.

- IMU model: the MVIS default fills fewer rows: its gyro and accel scale and cross-axis lanes say “no value”.
The MVIS (K-IMU) lane fills them, and the Leaderboard uses it on camera + IMU families.

## Configs

The pages do not show run configs now.
The config files are kept with the records in
calibench-vi/results (CC BY 4.0).
For each family and tool they hold:

- the command for one recording

- the settings

- what differs on the other recordings

Kalibr logs no command line. So we rebuild its camera-only commands from the settings the run passed.
The Basalt runs use our own headless build.

## Versioning

Each batch is dated and kept in the history of
calibench-vi/results.
So a comparison can be cited as “OpenMVIS leaderboard, batch 2026-11-24a, accessed <date>”.


---

# VI-Rig: 4 IMUs + 3 cameras results: MVIS, Kalibr and Basalt | OpenMVIS

URL: https://openmvis.com/benchmark/results/virig-4imus-3cams/

Photo: OpenMVIS

Our rig: a FLIR Blackfly and a RealSense T265 fisheye pair, all global shutter, with four IMUs from 100 to 500 Hz.
our data 3 global-shutter cameras 4 IMUs, 100–500 Hz
Batch 2026-11-24a · results commit 41ec486 · Leaderboard · Methodology
Dataset page: downloads Hugging Face: the data

Repeatability, not accuracy. There is no ground truth: a small spread shows that a tool repeats, not that
it is right, and a difference shows that two tools disagree, not which one is wrong. We ran every tool ourselves, including Kalibr and Basalt.

T6 · camera + IMU T6c · camera only

## T6 · camera + IMU

3 GS cameras + 4 IMUs · 10 recordings
Read first: Kalibr's intrinsics and baselines are inputs from its own camera-only calibration; its td and lever are solved given them. Data settings differ between the tools.

### Coverage

- MVIS 10 of 10
- Kalibr 10 of 10
- Basalt 0 of 10 not run: one IMU per run; no run holds the whole rig
MVIS made two runs per recording: its default IMU model ("MVIS") and Kalibr's IMU model ("MVIS (K-IMU)"), so the IMU terms of the second mean the same thing as Kalibr's.
Records behind these numbers: MVIS T6.json · Kalibr T6.json · Basalt T6.json
Fit: reprojection median, px (fit of each tool's own model, not accuracy)

# VI-Rig: 4 IMUs + 4 cameras results: MVIS, Kalibr and Basalt | OpenMVIS

URL: https://openmvis.com/benchmark/results/virig-4imus-4cams/

MVIS solve view, from the homepage

Our rig with a RealSense T265 fisheye pair (global shutter) and an ELP stereo pair (rolling shutter).
our data 2 global-shutter + 2 rolling-shutter cameras
Batch 2026-11-24a · results commit 41ec486 · Leaderboard · Methodology
Dataset page: downloads Device wiki: the device Hugging Face: the data

Repeatability, not accuracy. There is no ground truth: a small spread shows that a tool repeats, not that
it is right, and a difference shows that two tools disagree, not which one is wrong. We ran every tool ourselves, including Kalibr and Basalt.

T1 · camera only T2 · camera only T7 · camera + IMU T8 · camera + IMU

# VI-Rig: 5 IMUs + 4 cameras results: MVIS only | OpenMVIS

URL: https://openmvis.com/benchmark/results/virig-5imus-4cams/

Our rig with two RealSense T265 units (two global-shutter fisheye pairs) and five IMUs: an Xsens MTi as base, a GX3-25, a GX3-35 and the two T265 IMUs. A one-off MVIS study of 7 recordings, not part of the leaderboard batch or the regression suite. Kalibr and Basalt were not run on it.
our data 4 global-shutter fisheye cameras 5 IMUs, 100–500 Hz 7 recordings MVIS only
Separate study · batch 2026-11-02 · not part of the leaderboard batch
Example: how MVIS calibrates it Dataset page: downloads Device wiki: the device Hugging Face: the data

Repeatability, not accuracy. There is no ground truth: a small spread shows that a tool repeats, not that
it is right, and a difference shows that two tools disagree, not which one is wrong. We made every run ourselves; only MVIS was run on this set.

V5 · camera + IMU V5c · camera only

## Notes

- Two T265 units, one board. Each pair is hardware-synced inside its unit, but the two units are not synced to each other, so each camera-only solve holds one pair (time offset off). The camera + IMU solves hold all four cameras and five IMUs, and their intrinsics start from the 7-recording median of the camera-only solves.
- T265 IMU timing. The T265 IMUs' gyro–accel delay t_ga is about −6.6 ms, far from the other IMUs. MVIS estimates it per IMU; it is not a pure time shift (it depends on the motion's frequency), so read it as a compromise value.
- The results files (calibration numbers and run configs, no images) are on Hugging Face in calibench-vi/results, under runs/virig-5imus-4cams/2026-11-02/.

# TUM-VI results: MVIS, Kalibr and Basalt | OpenMVIS

URL: https://openmvis.com/benchmark/results/tum-vi/

MVIS solve view, from the homepage

The calibration bags of the TUM visual-inertial dataset: a global-shutter fisheye stereo pair and a BMI160 IMU.
2 global-shutter fisheye cameras, 20 Hz BMI160 IMU, 200 Hz AprilGrid 6×6, 88 mm
Batch 2026-11-24a · results commit 41ec486 · Leaderboard · Methodology
Example: how MVIS calibrates it Dataset page: downloads

Repeatability, not accuracy. There is no ground truth: a small spread shows that a tool repeats, not that
it is right, and a difference shows that two tools disagree, not which one is wrong. We ran every tool ourselves, including Kalibr and Basalt.

T3 · camera only T9 · camera + IMU T10 · camera + IMU

# Looper Insight 9 results: MVIS, Kalibr and Basalt | OpenMVIS

URL: https://openmvis.com/benchmark/results/looper-insight9/

Photo: LooperRobotics, Insight 9 product page

Two global-shutter cameras, one rolling-shutter camera and a MEMS IMU, from Looper Robotics.
2 global-shutter + 1 rolling-shutter camera MEMS IMU, 400 Hz AprilGrid 6×6, 55 mm
Batch 2026-11-24a · results commit 41ec486 · Leaderboard · Methodology
Example: how MVIS calibrates it Dataset page: downloads Device wiki: the device

Repeatability, not accuracy. There is no ground truth: a small spread shows that a tool repeats, not that
it is right, and a difference shows that two tools disagree, not which one is wrong. We ran every tool ourselves, including Kalibr and Basalt.

T4 · camera only T11 · camera + IMU

## T4 · camera only

Camera stereo · 10 recordings

### Coverage

- MVIS 10 of 10
- Kalibr 10 of 10
- Basalt 10 of 10
Records behind these numbers: MVIS T4.json · Kalibr T4.json · Basalt T4.json

# Monado MGC (HP Reverb G2) results: MVIS, Kalibr and Basalt | OpenMVIS

URL: https://openmvis.com/benchmark/results/monado-mgc/

Photo: HP, Reverb G2 press release

The MGC calibration recordings of the Monado SLAM Datasets, made with an HP Reverb G2 headset.
2 of the 4 headset cameras (front pair) headset IMU AprilGrid 6×6, 30 mm
Batch 2026-11-24a · results commit 41ec486 · Leaderboard · Methodology
Example: how MVIS calibrates it Dataset page: downloads Device wiki: the device Hugging Face: the data

Repeatability, not accuracy. There is no ground truth: a small spread shows that a tool repeats, not that
it is right, and a difference shows that two tools disagree, not which one is wrong. We ran every tool ourselves, including Kalibr and Basalt.

T5 · camera only T12 · camera + IMU

# UZH-FPV results: MVIS, Kalibr and Basalt | OpenMVIS

URL: https://openmvis.com/benchmark/results/uzh-fpv/

MVIS solve view, from the homepage

The camera–IMU calibration bags of the UZH-FPV Drone Racing dataset: an mDAVIS346 and a Snapdragon Flight, each recorded indoors and outdoors, at 45° and facing forward. A one-off study, not part of the leaderboard batch or the regression suite.
2 devices, 4 bags each AprilGrid 5×4, 75 mm
Separate study · batch 2026-11-04 · not part of the leaderboard batch
Example: how MVIS calibrates it Dataset page: downloads

Repeatability, not accuracy. There is no ground truth: a small spread shows that a tool repeats, not that
it is right, and a difference shows that two tools disagree, not which one is wrong. We ran every tool ourselves, including Kalibr and Basalt.

DAVIS · camera + IMU SNAP · camera + IMU

## Notes

- IMU weights. All three tools use IMU sigmas taken from the residuals in UZH's own Kalibr results, not the MVIS defaults. The example page explains how they are derived.
- One Basalt solve is left out. On davis_indoor_forward with these weights, Basalt gives a 120 mm lever and an accel scale (accelerometer scale factor) of 0.84. So its Davis column has 3 of 4 bags. At Basalt's default noise that bag is plausible, but snapdragon_indoor_45 then fails with a broken spline.
- Basalt's Davis distance stands out. Its camera-to-IMU distance is 33.6 mm. Kalibr gives 23.2 mm and MVIS 22.8 mm on the same 3 bags. We haven't established why. At default noise Basalt's lever z is 14–25 mm.
- Each device's 4 bags form one family, because the camera and IMU are on the same device. That assumes the camera–IMU geometry stayed the same across recordings, which we can't confirm.
- Snapdragon's time offset really does differ between bags, with an sd (standard deviation) near 4.7 ms in every tool. So a small difference between tools on that row says little about each bag.

## DAVIS · camera + IMU

mDAVIS346 + IMU · 4 recordings
Read first: All three tools use each bag's IMU weights from the residuals in UZH's own Kalibr results. Kalibr's intrinsics and baseline are inputs from the calibration UZH ships.

- Basalt 3 of 4

# Examples | OpenMVIS

URL: https://openmvis.com/benchmark/examples/

Each example is a complete calibration run on a released dataset. It shows:

- the configuration we used

- the result it produced

- how far the result is from a reference calibration, where one exists

Pick the one whose rig looks most like yours.

Looking for a specific device? See the Device wiki. All tools on all recordings? See the Leaderboard.

## How to read these pages

Every example page is laid out like a Device wiki page: a header card with the photo, the key facts and links, then the same sections in this order:

- Demo and values: what the page shows, the scene MVIS recovered from the dataset, and the run’s headline values.

- Calibration process: MVIS’s own player: the detected corners, then the rig’s path as the solve refines it.

- Solved rig: a 3D map of the solved rig and a table of every camera and IMU: intrinsics, lever arm, rotation as log(R), time offsets.

- Check against a reference: MVIS beside a published calibration and the difference, where one exists. Where none does, the page says so.

- Config and run: the run’s own config with the lines that matter marked and explained, the command, and what you need to get the same numbers.

- Dataset: the recording, its board drawn to scale, and where to download it.

Downloads are on each dataset’s own page, and comparisons across tools are on its results page.

Figures come from the run
The player, the map and the tables on each page are generated from the run they document. If a figure and the text disagree, the figure is right.

## Contributing an example

The most useful thing you can send is a run on a dataset we don’t have.

- For the format, see Submit a dataset.

- To add it to the Leaderboard as well, see Submit results.


---

# VI-Rig: 4 IMUs + 3 cameras | OpenMVIS

URL: https://openmvis.com/benchmark/examples/virig-4imus-3cams/

## Demo and values

One MVIS camera + IMU run on recording april_01: every camera and all four IMUs solved together.
The scene MVIS recovered from this dataset, as on the homepage. The values beside it come from this page's run.

Reprojection median 0.25 px
cam0–cam1 baseline 70.9 mm
cam0 td −4.32 ms
cam0 lever arm 91.6 mm

Reprojection is how far, in pixels, the detected corners lie from where the solve puts them. td is the camera–IMU time offset, and the lever arm is the camera–IMU position offset.

## Calibration process

MVIS's own player, from this run: the detected board corners, then the rig's path as the solve refines it. Press Play or drag the bar; pick a camera card to look through that camera. We publish no camera images.

## Solved rig

The solved positions and orientations, to scale in the IMU frame. Drag sideways to orbit. Tap a sensor to see its values.

Sensor | fx, fy, cx, cy px | Lever mm | log(R) rad | td ms | t_ga ms | Reprojection px |
cam0 | 448.1, 447.5, 371.8, 280.9 | [+32.6, −80.9, +27.9] | [+0.0031, −2.2167, +2.2213] | −4.32 | | 0.293 |
cam1 | 286.8, 286.4, 415.7, 403.0 | [+66.4, −111.0, −26.7] | [+0.0179, +2.2310, −2.2116] | −5.01 | | 0.213 |
cam2 | 286.7, 286.1, 415.2, 397.4 | [+2.5, −110.4, −26.6] | [−0.0255, −2.2258, +2.2122] | −7.68 | | 0.226 |
IMU (base) | | 0 | 0 | 0 | −0.28 ± 0.04 | |
IMU gx3_25 | | [−122.5, −47.0, −3.2] | [+2.2382, +2.2040, −0.0239] | +0.00 | +0.18 ± 0.03 | |

The marked lines are the choices that matter for this rig:

- gravity: Kept at 9.81 m/s² for Newark, DE (Univ. of Delaware): the local gravity there, 9.8013 m/s², differs from it by under 0.1 %. Set your own local value.
- site: The alternative to gravity: the recording site. With gravity set it does not change g; it names the city in the report.
- input.imu_topics: Four IMU topics. The first is the base IMU; the other three are solved against it.
- input.window_mode: MVIS picks the 80 s window with the most motion.
- camera_input.cameras: The two T265 cameras are added to the graph at 4 Hz, which keeps the solve small.
- solve.sigma_g: IMU noise from a still recording of this rig, measured density × 2.5. The other three sigmas are set the same way.
- estimate.board_points: The printed board is not quite flat, so its shape is estimated too.
- estimate.camera.intrinsics: Camera intrinsics stay free in the camera + IMU solve.
This is the config of the run on this page, with every path cut to its file name; the gravity line gives the g the run used. Point the paths at your copy, and take the gravity for your site from the Local gravity page.

## Dataset

- Recording april_01, one of the 10 recordings of this rig. MVIS picks the 80 s window with the most motion.
- Cameras: a Blackfly S (pinhole with radial-tangential distortion) and the two T265 fisheye cameras (equidistant lens model).
- IMUs: the Xsens MTi is the base IMU; the two MicroStrain units and the T265's own IMU are solved against it.

# VI-Rig: 4 IMUs + 4 cameras | OpenMVIS

One MVIS camera + IMU run on recording 4imus_4cams_01: all four cameras and all four IMUs solved together.

Reprojection median 0.25 px
cam0–cam1 baseline 63.7 mm
cam0 td −5.41 ms
cam0 lever arm 130.8 mm

Reprojection is how far, in pixels, the detected corners lie from where the solve puts them. td is the camera–IMU time offset, and the lever arm is the camera–IMU position offset.

## Calibration process

MVIS's own player, from this run: the detected board corners, then the rig's path as the solve refines it. Press Play or drag the bar; pick a camera card to look through that camera. We publish no camera images.

The marked lines are the choices that matter for this rig:

- gravity: Kept at 9.81 m/s² for Newark, DE (Univ. of Delaware): the local gravity there, 9.8013 m/s², differs from it by under 0.1 %. Set your own local value.
- site: The alternative to gravity: the recording site. With gravity set it does not change g; it names the city in the report.
- input.imu_topics: Four IMU topics. The first is the base IMU; the other three are solved against it.
- input.window_mode: MVIS picks the 80 s window with the most motion.
- camera_input.cameras: The ELP cameras are rolling shutter, so their readout time is estimated. The three cameras after the first are added to the graph at 4 Hz, which keeps the solve small.
- solve.sigma_g: The same IMU noise values as the 3-camera example, which has the same Xsens base IMU.
- estimate.board_points: The printed board is not quite flat, so its shape is estimated too.
- estimate.camera.intrinsics: Camera intrinsics stay free in the camera + IMU solve.

The marked lines are the choices that matter for this rig:

- camera_input.path: The starting camera intrinsics, from camera-only solves of all 7 recordings.

- estimate.board_points: The printed board is not quite flat, so its shape is estimated too.
- estimate.camera.intrinsics: Camera intrinsics stay free in the camera + IMU solve.

- Cameras: the fisheye pairs of two T265 units, all global shutter, with the equidistant lens model. Each pair is synced inside its unit, but the two units are not synced to each other; their time offsets are solved against the base IMU.
- IMUs: the Xsens MTi is the base IMU; the two MicroStrain units and the two T265 IMUs are solved against it.
- Board: AprilGrid 6×6, tag 88 mm, spacing 0.3, t36h11.

# TUM-VI | OpenMVIS

URL: https://openmvis.com/benchmark/examples/tum-vi/

## Demo and values

One MVIS camera + IMU run on dataset-calib-imu1, and how close it lands to TUM's published Kalibr calibration.
The scene MVIS recovered from this dataset, as on the homepage. The values beside it come from this page's run.

Reprojection median 0.10 px
cam0–cam1 baseline 101.1 mm
cam0 td +0.17 ms
cam0 lever arm 94.7 mm

Reprojection is how far, in pixels, the detected corners lie from where the solve puts them. td is the camera–IMU time offset, and the lever arm is the camera–IMU position offset.

## Calibration process

MVIS's own player, from this run: the detected board corners, then the rig's path as the solve refines it. Press Play or drag the bar; pick a camera card to look through that camera. We publish no camera images.

## Solved rig

The solved positions and orientations, to scale in the IMU frame. Drag sideways to orbit. Tap a sensor to see its values.

Sensor | fx, fy, cx, cy px | Lever mm | log(R) rad | td ms | t_ga ms | Reprojection px |
cam0 | 382.8, 382.8, 509.9, 514.2 | [+46.4, −68.9, −45.5] | [−0.0514, −2.1752, +2.2543] | +0.17 | | 0.099 |
cam1 | 381.4, 381.4, 505.3, 510.2 | [−54.7, −67.4, −49.0] | [−0.0517, −2.2279, +2.2019] | +0.17 | | 0.093 |
IMU (base) | | 0 | 0 | 0 | −1.57 ± 0.30 | |

Lever arms and rotations are each sensor in the base IMU frame; rotation is log(R) in rad. td is the time offset to the base IMU, t_imu = t_sensor + td. Reprojection is the median per camera (all cameras: median 0.096 px): how well the model fits the corners, not how accurate it is.

## Check against a reference

Reference: TUM's published camera + IMU calibration for the 1024 × 1024 data, Kalibr pinhole-equidistant (the kb4 model), from the TUM-VI dataset page.
Value | MVIS | TUM (Kalibr) | Difference |
cam0 |
Lever mm | [+46.36, −68.92, −45.48] | [+45.38, −72.68, −45.07] | Δp 3.91 mm |
log(R) rad | [−0.0514, −2.1752, +2.2543] | [−0.0413, −2.1724, +2.2481] | Δθ 9.28 mrad |
fx px | 382.77 | 380.81 | Δfx +1.96 px |
td ms | +0.169 | not in TUM's calibration file | |
cam1 |
Lever mm | [−54.71, −67.39, −48.97] | [−55.52, −71.10, −47.83] | Δp 3.96 mm |
log(R) rad | [−0.0517, −2.2279, +2.2019] | [−0.0417, −2.2243, +2.1962] | Δθ 9.25 mrad |
fx px | 381.36 | 379.29 | Δfx +2.07 px |
td ms | +0.168 | not in TUM's calibration file | |

Δp is the distance between the two lever arms. Δθ = ‖log(RaT Rb)‖, the angle between the two rotations. A reference, not ground truth: it was solved by another tool on the same kind of data.
The rotation differs by about 9.4 mrad on both cameras. That offset is systematic: MVIS gives the same rotation on all four TUM calibration recordings. It is not explained yet. One possible cause, not verified: this run uses the raw IMU, while TUM's Kalibr run used an IMU model it had already calibrated, so the two IMU frames may differ by a small rotation.
Lens model note: on these lenses the kb4 polynomial folds back inside the image, past about 114° (682 px from the centre) on cam0 and 119° (705 px) on cam1. The model gives no ray beyond that radius.

The marked lines are the choices that matter for this rig:

- gravity: Kept at 9.81 m/s² for TUM Garching, Germany: the local gravity there, 9.8077 m/s², differs from it by under 0.1 %. Set your own local value.
- site: The alternative to gravity: the recording site. With gravity set it does not change g; it names the city in the report.
- input.window_mode: MVIS picks the 80 s window with the most motion; a shorter recording is used whole.
- camera_input.path: Seed intrinsics: kb4 values from MVIS camera-only solves of TUM's eight camera recordings.
- camera_input.cameras: cam1 is added to the graph at 8 Hz, which keeps the solve small.
- solve.estimate_t_ga: Estimates t_ga, the time offset between the gyroscope and the accelerometer.
- estimate.camera.intrinsics: Camera intrinsics stay free in the camera + IMU solve.
- estimate.imu: The gyro and accelerometer scale and misalignment (dw_da) are estimated too. IMU noise is left at the MVIS defaults.
This is the config of the run on this page, with every path cut to its file name; the gravity line gives the g the run used. Point the paths at your copy, and take the gravity for your site from the Local gravity page.
The solve took about 10 min on one desktop. It writes cam_imu.json, a calibration YAML and a report beside the config.

Run date: 2026-11-24

# Monado: HP Reverb G2 | OpenMVIS

URL: https://openmvis.com/benchmark/examples/monado/

## Demo and values

One MVIS camera + IMU run on the HP Reverb G2 recording imucalib01 (round 1), and how close it lands to the calibration Monado ships with the data.
The scene MVIS recovered from this dataset, as on the homepage. The values beside it come from this page's run.

Reprojection median 0.13 px
cam0–cam1 baseline 108.5 mm
cam0 td −1.22 ms
cam0 lever arm 53.9 mm

Reprojection is how far, in pixels, the detected corners lie from where the solve puts them. td is the camera–IMU time offset, and the lever arm is the camera–IMU position offset.

## Calibration process

MVIS's own player, from this run: the detected board corners, then the rig's path as the solve refines it. Press Play or drag the bar; pick a camera card to look through that camera. We publish no camera images.

## Solved rig

The solved positions and orientations, to scale in the IMU frame. Drag sideways to orbit. Tap a sensor to see its values.

Sensor | fx, fy, cx, cy px | Lever mm | log(R) rad | td ms | t_ga ms | Reprojection px |
cam0 | 269.9, 270.2, 322.5, 229.2 | [−52.0, +13.4, +5.3] | [−0.3460, +0.0755, +1.5382] | −1.22 | | 0.121 |
cam1 | 268.9, 268.8, 323.8, 237.0 | [+56.5, +14.2, +5.5] | [−0.0750, +0.3458, +1.5941] | −1.21 | | 0.138 |
IMU (base) | | 0 | 0 | 0 | +2.50 ± 0.21 | |

Lever arms and rotations are each sensor in the base IMU frame; rotation is log(R) in rad. td is the time offset to the base IMU, t_imu = t_sensor + td. Reprojection is the median per camera (all cameras: median 0.130 px): how well the model fits the corners, not how accurate it is.

## Check against a reference

Reference: The Basalt calibration Monado ships with the HP Reverb G2 data (MG_reverb_g2, extras, calibration).
Value | MVIS | Monado (Basalt) | Difference |
cam0 |
Lever mm | [−51.97, +13.44, +5.31] | [−51.95, +12.66, +5.70] | Δp 0.87 mm |
log(R) rad | [−0.3460, +0.0755, +1.5382] | [−0.3456, +0.0756, +1.5383] | Δθ 0.35 mrad |
fx px | 269.91 | not comparable: Basalt used an 8-parameter radial-tangential lens | |
td ms | −1.221 | fixed at 0 in that file, not an estimate | |
cam1 |
Lever mm | [+56.52, +14.18, +5.50] | [+56.45, +13.37, +5.82] | Δp 0.87 mm |
log(R) rad | [−0.0750, +0.3458, +1.5941] | [−0.0726, +0.3445, +1.5945] | Δθ 2.51 mrad |
fx px | 268.87 | not comparable: Basalt used an 8-parameter radial-tangential lens | |
td ms | −1.213 | fixed at 0 in that file, not an estimate | |

Δp is the distance between the two lever arms. Δθ = ‖log(RaT Rb)‖, the angle between the two rotations. A reference, not ground truth: it was solved by another tool on the same kind of data.
Monado ships a second, equidistant calibration of the same headset. Its rotations differ from this file's by about 4.5 mrad, so a few mrad is within how much the references themselves disagree.

## Config and run

monado_mgc_imucalib01_cam_imu.yaml
gravity : 9.7931 # m/s², Córdoba, Argentina

site :

latitude_deg : -31.42

longitude_deg : -64.18

altitude_m : 400

name : Córdoba, Argentina

input :

format : euroc

path : MGC04_imucalib01_1/mav0

cam_topics :

- cam0

- cam1

imu_topics :

- imu0

window_mode : motion

segment_length : 80.0

board :

board_type : apriltag

rows : 6

cols : 6

tag_size : 0.03

tag_spacing : 0.3

tag_family : t36h11

heights_file : null

camera_input :

path : camera_prior.yaml

cameras :

- estimate_readout : false

- estimate_readout : false

factor_hz : 8.0

solve :

max_iterations : 40

pnp_method : ippe

corner_subsample : all

estimate_t_ga : true

sigma_t_ga : 0.01

vision_pose : imu

estimate :

camera :

intrinsics : true

tr : false

td : true

extrinsics : true

imu :

intrinsics : dw_da

model : calyx

output :

path : cam_imu.json

shell
mvis cam-imu -c monado_mgc_imucalib01_cam_imu.yaml

The marked lines are the choices that matter for this rig:

- gravity: The local gravity in Córdoba, Argentina, where it was recorded: 9.7931 m/s², 0.17 % below 9.81. With 9.81 the accel scale would read 0.17 % high.
- site: The alternative to gravity: the recording site. MVIS computes the same 9.7931 m/s² from it, and the report names the city.
- board.tag_size: The 30 mm tag. A wrong tag size gives a calibration that converges cleanly and is uniformly wrong in scale.
- input.window_mode: MVIS picks the 80 s window with the most motion; a shorter recording is used whole.
- camera_input.cameras: cam1 is added to the graph at 8 Hz, which keeps the solve small.
- solve.estimate_t_ga: Estimates t_ga, the time offset between the gyroscope and the accelerometer.
- estimate.camera.intrinsics: Camera intrinsics stay free in the camera + IMU solve.
This is the config of the run on this page, with every path cut to its file name; the gravity line gives the g the run used. Point the paths at your copy, and take the gravity for your site from the Local gravity page.
The solve took about 7 min on one desktop. It writes cam_imu.json, a calibration YAML and a report beside the config.
MVIS: MVIS 0.4.0, re-solve of 2026-11-24
Run date: 2026-11-24
Data: Monado SLAM Datasets
Config: monado_mgc_imucalib01_cam_imu.yaml, above
Command: mvis cam-imu -c monado_mgc_imucalib01_cam_imu.yaml

## Dataset

- Recording MGC imucalib01, round 1, from the Monado SLAM Datasets (Collabora). It shows the board to the front camera pair, cam0 and cam1.
- Cameras: 640 × 480 grayscale at 30 Hz, fitted with the equidistant lens model, as in the MVIS regression config for this headset. IMU at about 1 kHz.
- Board: AprilGrid 6×6, tag 30 mm, spacing 0.3, t36h11. The tag is much smaller than the usual 88 mm, and board size scales every translation.
- Solve window: 41.6 s.
Download: Monado SLAM Datasets The recordings are listed there, not copied here.

AprilGrid 6 × 6, 225 × 225 mm. Standard pattern, to scale

## More on this data

- Monado SLAM Datasets
- All recordings and tools: results page
- HP Reverb G2 in the Device wiki
The other two camera pairs Device wiki
The headset has four cameras, and each recording shows the board to one pair. The sensor page stitches all four together from three pair recordings. HP Reverb G2

t_ga on and off Why calibrate t_ga
This run estimates t_ga, the time offset between the gyroscope and the accelerometer, as every MVIS camera + IMU run does by default. What happens to tools that cannot model it is shown on its own page. Why calibrate t_ga

The marked lines are the choices that matter for this rig:

- gravity: The local gravity in Shenzhen, China, where it was recorded: 9.7879 m/s², 0.23 % below 9.81. With 9.81 the accel scale would read 0.23 % high.
- site: The alternative to gravity: the recording site. MVIS computes the same 9.7879 m/s² from it, and the report names the city.
- camera_input.free_intrinsics: Camera intrinsics stay free in the camera + IMU solve.
- camera_input.cameras: The colour camera (cam2) has a rolling shutter, so its readout time is estimated.
- solve.estimate_t_ga: Estimates t_ga, the time offset between the gyroscope and the accelerometer.
- solve.sigma_g: IMU noise from a still recording of this unit, measured density × 2.5. The other three sigmas are set the same way.

## Config and run

uzh_fpv_snapdragon_outdoor_forward_cam_imu.yaml
gravity : 9.81 # m/s², Innovation Park Zürich, Dübendorf, Switzerland; local 9.8070, under 0.1 %

latitude_deg : 47.4

longitude_deg : 8.62

altitude_m : 440

- /snappy_imu

board_type : apriltag

rows : 4

cols : 5

tag_size : 0.075

tag_spacing : 0.2

tag_family : t36h11

camera_input :

path : camera_prior_kalibr_camchain.yaml

estimate_readout : false

solve :

imu_intrinsics : dw_da

estimate_t_ga : true

sigma_g : 0.0002999232700379165

sigma_a : 0.0025286614063113116

sigma_bg : 2.9992327003791653e-05

sigma_ba : 0.00025286614063113117

output :

path : cam_imu.json

shell
mvis cam-imu -c uzh_fpv_snapdragon_outdoor_forward_cam_imu.yaml

The marked lines are the choices that matter for this rig:

- gravity: Kept at 9.81 m/s² for Innovation Park Zürich, Dübendorf, Switzerland: the local gravity there, 9.8070 m/s², differs from it by under 0.1 %. Set your own local value.
- site: The alternative to gravity: the recording site. With gravity set it does not change g; it names the city in the report.
- board: The UZH board: AprilGrid 5×4, tag 75 mm, spacing 0.2.
- camera_input.path: Seed intrinsics: UZH's own camera-only Kalibr calibration, equidistant lens. MVIS refines them in this solve.
- solve.sigma_g: IMU noise from the residuals of UZH's own Kalibr results, as UZH publishes no measured density. The other three sigmas are set the same way.
- solve.estimate_t_ga: Estimates t_ga, the time offset between the gyroscope and the accelerometer.
This is the config of the run on this page, with every path cut to its file name; the gravity line gives the g the run used. Point the paths at your copy, and take the gravity for your site from the Local gravity page.
The solve took about 5 min on one desktop. It writes cam_imu.json, a calibration YAML and a report beside the config.
MVIS: MVIS 0.4.0, re-solve of 2026-11-24
Run date: 2026-11-24
Data: UZH-FPV datasets page
Config: uzh_fpv_snapdragon_outdoor_forward_cam_imu.yaml, above
Command: mvis cam-imu -c uzh_fpv_snapdragon_outdoor_forward_cam_imu.yaml

## Dataset

- Recording outdoor_forward_calib_snapdragon: the Snapdragon Flight's two 640 × 480 global-shutter cameras, fitted with the equidistant lens model as in UZH's own calibration, and its IMU at about 500 Hz.
- IMU noise: UZH publishes no measured noise density, so the sigmas come from the residuals of UZH's own Kalibr results. They are estimates.
- Board: AprilGrid 5×4, tag 75 mm, spacing 0.2, t36h11.
- Cite Delmerico et al., "Are We Ready for Autonomous Drone Racing? The UZH-FPV Drone Racing Dataset", ICRA 2019. Licence: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0.
- Solve window: 44.7 s.
Download: UZH-FPV datasets page The recordings are listed there, not copied here.

AprilGrid 4 × 5, 435 × 345 mm. Standard pattern, to scale

# Device wiki | OpenMVIS

URL: https://openmvis.com/devices/

Cameras, IMUs and rigs we calibrated with MVIS, one page per device. Each page has the same sections:

- Demo and values

- Calibration process

- Solved rig

- Specifications

- Dataset

- Detailed results

- Limits

- How it was run

Tracking modules · Head-worn cameras · VR headsets · 360° cameras

## Tracking modules

- Intel RealSense T265 Tracking camera: global-shutter fisheye stereo with a Bosch BMI055 IMU OmniVision OV9282 ×2 Bosch BMI055 Global shutter 2 cameras 200 Hz IMU

- RealSense D455 Depth camera: global-shutter infrared stereo and RGB with a 6-axis IMU OmniVision OV9782 ×3 Bosch BMI055 / BMI085 Global shutter 3 cameras 400 Hz IMU

- RealSense D456 Depth camera: global-shutter infrared stereo and RGB with a 6-axis IMU OmniVision OV9782 ×3 Bosch BMI085 Global shutter 3 cameras 400 Hz IMU

- RealSense D435i Depth camera: global-shutter infrared stereo, rolling-shutter RGB and a 6-axis IMU OmniVision OV2740 OmniVision OV9282 ×2 Bosch BMI055 / BMI085 Global + rolling shutter 3 cameras 200 Hz IMU

- RoboBaton Neo VIO module: global-shutter fisheye camera with a TDK ICM-42670-P IMU SmartSens SC132GS TDK InvenSense ICM-42670-P Global shutter 1 camera 200 Hz IMU

- Stereolabs ZED 2 Stereo depth camera: two rolling-shutter cameras with a 400 Hz IMU OmniVision OV4689 ×2 Bosch BMI270 Rolling shutter 2 cameras 400 Hz IMU

- LooperRobotics Insight 9 Spatial AI camera: stereo pair, rolling-shutter colour camera, 6-axis IMU, VIO SmartSens SC132GS ×2 Sony IMX415 Bosch BMI088 Global + rolling shutter 3 cameras 400 Hz IMU

Tracking camera from Intel with two global-shutter fisheye cameras and a Bosch BMI055 IMU, solved here on its own IMU from one recording of our VI-Rig.

Reprojection median 0.16 px
cam0–cam1 baseline 63.8 mm
cam0 td −8.00 ms
cam0 lever arm 14.8 mm

Reprojection is how far, in pixels, the detected corners lie from where the solve puts them. td is the camera–IMU time offset, and the lever arm is the camera–IMU position offset.
One recording, with no independent reference on this page. These values show what MVIS solved, not how close they are to the truth.

## Limits

- One recording, with no independent reference on this page. These values show what MVIS solved, not how close they are to the truth.
- The T265 gyro-to-accel offset isn't a pure time shift. We measured about −6.8 ms at 2–4 Hz and −1.2 ms at 30–40 Hz, so a single t_ga is a compromise that depends on the motion.

## How it was run

- Fisheye stereo plus the T265's own IMU, camera intrinsics free, t_ga estimated, and the shape of the calibration board estimated, since the VI-Rig board isn't perfectly flat: about 4.5 mm peak to peak in this August 2021 recording (see Board shape); later recordings of the same board design, from October 2021, show the same saddle at 10–11 mm. Solved 2026-11-12.

## Limits

- One recording, with no independent reference on this page. These values show what MVIS solved, not how close they are to the truth.
- The square size, 75 mm, is the recorder's measurement of the board shown on a screen, and it scales every baseline and lever arm. The solved stereo baseline is about 0.7 % under the 95 mm the maker lists.
- The infrared images are the camera's own rectified output, so their distortion is close to zero by construction and the values describe that output, not the bare lens.
- The recorder turned the camera's IMU correction off, so the IMU scale and bias values are those of the raw sensor. The accelerometer was resampled onto the gyro's time stamps before the solve.

## How it was run

- Left infrared, right infrared and RGB cameras with the IMU in one solve, all three treated as global shutter. Pinhole camera with radial-tangential distortion, seeded from three single-camera solves of the same recording and left free; camera time offsets, IMU scale and misalignment and the gyro-to-accel offset t_ga estimated. The board is kept rigid. IMU noise is the MVIS default, since no measured values exist for this unit. Solved 2026-11-13.


---

# RealSense D435i camera–IMU calibration | OpenMVIS

URL: https://openmvis.com/devices/realsense-d435i/

## Demo and values

Depth camera from RealSense with a 50 mm global-shutter infrared stereo pair, a rolling-shutter RGB camera and a 6-axis IMU. Four hand-held recordings in front of an AprilGrid; the first, 95 s long, is shown here, solved as RGB + left infrared + right infrared + IMU with the RGB rolling-shutter readout estimated.
The 3D scene MVIS recovered from an earlier RGB-only recording of the same camera (2026-11-13).

Reprojection median 0.08 px
cam0–cam1 baseline 14.6 mm
cam0 td, first row +6.26 ms +22.46 ms at mid-frame
cam0 lever arm 30.4 mm

Reprojection is how far, in pixels, the detected corners lie from where the solve puts them. td is the camera–IMU time offset, and the lever arm is the camera–IMU position offset.
We ran the same solve on all four recordings. They agree on the RGB lever arm across the image (x within 0.3 mm), the time offset (within 0.08 ms), the readout time (32.33 to 32.42 ms), the focal length (within 1.2 px) and the infrared baseline (49.98 to 50.08 mm, against the 50.05 mm stored in the camera). They do not agree along the optical axis: the RGB lever z is 17.7 to 21.8 mm, a 4.1 mm spread, and every camera sits 6 to 10 mm above the RealSense SDK's design values. The infrared cameras spread as much as the RGB camera, so the rolling shutter is not the cause. All four recordings turn the camera little about the axes across the image, which is what makes that distance observable, so z is not settled.

## Calibration process

The path of the rig around the board, as MVIS solved it. To explore it:

- Press Play or drag the bar to follow the path.
- Use the view buttons to change the view.
- Pick a camera card to put that camera on the frustum, the pyramid that shows its view.
Each card draws the board from the solved pose, with the corners MVIS detected. We publish no camera images.

cam1 | −8.4, +6.5, +18.8 | 21.6 | [+0.001, −0.003, +0.005] | +6.32 | 79° × 64° |

## Limits

- We ran the same solve on all four recordings. They agree on the RGB lever arm across the image (x within 0.3 mm), the time offset (within 0.08 ms), the readout time (32.33 to 32.42 ms), the focal length (within 1.2 px) and the infrared baseline (49.98 to 50.08 mm, against the 50.05 mm stored in the camera). They do not agree along the optical axis: the RGB lever z is 17.7 to 21.8 mm, a 4.1 mm spread, and every camera sits 6 to 10 mm above the RealSense SDK's design values. The infrared cameras spread as much as the RGB camera, so the rolling shutter is not the cause. All four recordings turn the camera little about the axes across the image, which is what makes that distance observable, so z is not settled.
- The tag size, 88 mm, is the stated size of the printed board, and it scales every lever arm and baseline.
- The board is not flat: its corners lie 6.4 to 7.1 mm peak to peak out of plane over the four recordings.
- The camera stores no IMU correction, so the IMU scale and bias values are those of the raw sensor. IMU noise is the MVIS default, and the gyro's sensitivity to acceleration is not estimated.
- The infrared distortion comes out close to zero, as expected if the camera delivers rectified infrared images, so those values describe that output, not the bare lens.

## How it was run

- Each camera first solved on its own, then the RGB and both infrared cameras with the IMU in one solve. The RGB camera is a rolling-shutter camera with the readout time estimated; the infrared pair is global shutter. Pinhole cameras with radial-tangential distortion, seeded from the single-camera solves and left free; the camera time offsets, IMU scale and misalignment and the gyro-to-accel offset t_ga estimated. The board shape is estimated per corner. IMU noise is the MVIS default, since no measured values exist for this unit. Gravity is the local value at the recording site, 9.7892 m/s² (UAE). Solved 2026-11-24.


---

# RoboBaton Neo camera–IMU calibration | OpenMVIS

URL: https://openmvis.com/devices/robobaton-neo/

## Demo and values

Small VIO module from RoboBaton, 8.7 g on a 40 × 20 mm board, with one global-shutter fisheye camera and a TDK ICM-42670-P IMU, hardware-triggered. One hand-held recording in front of an AprilGrid shown on a monitor, recorded by the module's own capture tool and solved as camera + IMU.
The 3D scene MVIS recovered from the recording.

Reprojection median 0.41 px
cam0 td +1.14 ms
cam0 lever arm 31.1 mm

Reprojection is how far, in pixels, the detected corners lie from where the solve puts them. td is the camera–IMU time offset, and the lever arm is the camera–IMU position offset.
One recording, 5 frames per second. The maker's own calibration of the same recording agrees on the rotation (within 0.4°) and on the lever arm across the image (within 2 mm), but not along the optical axis (17 mm here against 9 mm) nor on the time offset (1.1 ms against 0.3 ms). A digital twin of the recording puts the noise on z at about 1 mm, so the gap is systematic; the image stamp convention and the tag size on the monitor are the open questions.

## Calibration process

The path of the rig around the board, as MVIS solved it. To explore it:

- Press Play or drag the bar to follow the path.
- Use the view buttons to change the view.
- Pick a camera card to put that camera on the frustum, the pyramid that shows its view.
Each card draws the board from the solved pose, with the corners MVIS detected. We publish no camera images.

## Limits

- One recording, 5 frames per second. The maker's own calibration of the same recording agrees on the rotation (within 0.4°) and on the lever arm across the image (within 2 mm), but not along the optical axis (17 mm here against 9 mm) nor on the time offset (1.1 ms against 0.3 ms). A digital twin of the recording puts the noise on z at about 1 mm, so the gap is systematic; the image stamp convention and the tag size on the monitor are the open questions.
- The tag size, 25 mm, is the value in the capture tool's config, not a measurement on the monitor; it scales the lever arm.
- A double-sphere model fits as well as kb4, but its focal length and xi trade off along a flat valley, so only the projection is comparable between the two.

## How it was run

- Camera with the IMU in one solve. Kannala-Brandt (kb4) fisheye intrinsics seeded from a single-camera solve of the same recording and left free; the camera time offset, IMU scale and misalignment and the gyro-to-accel offset t_ga estimated. The board shape is estimated per corner. IMU noise is the ICM-42670-P datasheet value times three. Solved 2026-11-19.

## Limits

- No independent reference. The authors publish a Kalibr calibration from the same recording with a global-shutter camera model; it isn't an independent check.
- The time offset is given at the first image row. At mid-image, the time a global-shutter model reports, it is about 7 ms later (+4.5 ms).
- The board is small (about 15 cm), so the image edges are covered less well and the principal point trades with the lens distortion: a Kannala–Brandt model moves it by about 10 px with no change in fit.
- The recording runs at 19.7 Hz and the IMU at 381 Hz, below the 30 fps and 400 Hz on the sheet, probably from drops while recording.

## How it was run

- Both cameras and the IMU together. Camera intrinsics (pinhole with radial-tangential distortion, as in the authors' calibration) start from a camera-only solve and stay free; rolling-shutter readout, camera time offsets, IMU scale and misalignment and the gyro-to-accel offset t_ga are estimated. IMU noise from the authors' IMU file. Solved 2026-11-16.

The time offsets, to scale. td is the camera–IMU time offset, with t_imu = t_cam + td. For a rolling-shutter camera td is the time of the first image row; the middle row is td + readout / 2, which is what a global-shutter calibration reports.

Board shape peak to peak 0.6 mm
The calibration board isn't perfectly flat, so this solve estimated the height of every corner off the flat board along with the calibration. The board's mean plane and tilt belong to its pose, so a flat board shows only noise here.
Height of each corner off the flat board: peak to peak 0.6 mm, rms 0.1 mm. Numbers are the corner column and row (row 0 at the bottom). Hover or tap a corner for its value.

## Limits

- No reference exists for these recordings, so the values can't be checked for accuracy.
- Hand-held and robot-arm recordings are kept apart, not pooled. They were solved in different batches and may not come from the same unit.
- The arm program rotates mostly about one axis, which leaves lever arms less well determined, so treat the arm's values with more caution.
- The chessboard recordings come from our own unit, not the partner's, and are shown on their own. The values shown come from take 04 alone, so they show no repeatability; all 4 takes are in the hosted data.

## How it was run

- Camera + IMU with camera intrinsics free, t_ga and the cam2 rolling-shutter readout both estimated. Chessboard recordings of 2026-11-07; hand-held batch of 2026-11-02; robot-arm batch of 2026-11-04.

# Dibuli Prism-A4L camera–IMU calibration | OpenMVIS

URL: https://openmvis.com/devices/dibuli-prism-a4l/

## Demo and values

Multi-sensor capture box from Dibuli with four global-shutter fisheye cameras and a 6-axis IMU, solved from the maker's public example data at two exposures.
The 3D scene MVIS recovered from the maker's example data, 1,000 µs exposure.

Reprojection median 0.18 px
cam0–cam1 baseline 85.3 mm
cam0 td +2.07 ms
cam0 lever arm 71.7 mm

Reprojection median 0.18 px
cam0–cam1 baseline 85.3 mm
cam0 td +2.66 ms
cam0 lever arm 71.8 mm

Reprojection is how far, in pixels, the detected corners lie from where the solve puts them. td is the camera–IMU time offset, and the lever arm is the camera–IMU position offset.
No independent reference on this page. These values show what MVIS solved, not how close they are to the truth.

## Calibration process

The path of the rig around the board, as MVIS solved it. To explore it:

- Press Play or drag the bar to follow the path.
- Use the view buttons to change the view.
- Pick a camera card to put that camera on the frustum, the pyramid that shows its view.
Each card draws the board from the solved pose, with the corners MVIS detected. We publish no camera images.

## Solved rig

The solved rig in 3D, to scale. Tap a sensor to see its values. In full screen you can rotate and zoom. Grid squares are 20 mm.

## Limits

- No independent reference, so these values show what MVIS solved, not how close they are to the truth.
- We solved three recordings of the same unit separately. The lever arm agrees within 2.5 mm, the camera-to-IMU time offset within 0.25 ms, the focal lengths within 1.3 px and the IMU scales within 0.45 %. The IMU position also agrees with the maker's drawing within 2 mm.
- The board reaches about 54° off-axis. Past that, toward the image edges (61°) and corners (72°), the lens model is extrapolated: the three solves differ by up to 7 px at the edges and 35 px at the corners.
- The motion is gentle (about 6 to 11°/s RMS). In a simulated copy of each recording, with noise matched to this unit, MVIS recovered the lever arm within 1.1 mm, the rotation within 0.6 mrad, the time offset within 0.1 ms and the IMU scales within 0.4 %. The solver's own σ for the lever arm (2 to 4 mm) is wider, because the solve used MVIS's default IMU noise, which is looser than this IMU needs.
- The model is matched from resolution, baseline, field of view and shutter, not confirmed by the maker.

## How it was run

- Both cameras and the IMU, global shutter, default IMU noise, t_ga estimated, camera intrinsics free. The IMU stored accel 4× and gyro 2× too small; both were scaled before solving. Solved 2026-11-21 with MVIS 0.3.0, which reads the ChArUco board natively; cx and cy are about 0.45 px lower than in the first solve of 2026-11-11.

# ALG AVS115D-Y stereo module camera–IMU calibration | OpenMVIS

URL: https://openmvis.com/devices/alg-avs115d/

## Demo and values

GMSL2 stereo camera module from Shenzhen Aili-Light Technology (ALG Tech, 艾利光), with two 1920×1920 rolling-shutter cameras 65 mm apart and a 6-axis IMU. Reprojection is how far, in pixels, the detected corners lie from where the solve puts them. td is the camera–IMU time offset, and the lever arm is the camera–IMU position offset.

The path of the rig around the board, as MVIS solved it. To explore it:

- Press Play or drag the bar to follow the path.
- Use the view buttons to change the view.
- Pick a camera card to put that camera on the frustum, the pyramid that shows its view.
Each card draws the board from the solved pose, with the corners MVIS detected. We publish no camera images.

## Limits

- No independent reference on this page. These values show what MVIS solved, not how close they are to the truth. The two recordings agree within 1.5 mm on the lever arm, 0.15 % on the gyro scales, 0.9 ms on the readout and 0.1 mm on the baseline.
- The camera-only solve, without the IMU, puts the readout at 25 ms (recording 1) and 21 ms (recording 2) against 31–32 ms here; the board's motion alone pins it less well, so the joint value is the one shown.
- In a simulated copy of recording 1, with noise matched to this unit, MVIS recovered the lever arm within 1.2 mm, the rotation within 0.3 mrad, the time offset within 0.5 ms, the readout within 0.6 ms and the gyro scales within 0.7 %. With MVIS's default IMU noise the same test drifts (lever arm 6 mm along the optical axis, gyro scales 1 to 1.6 %), which is why this solve uses the tighter noise.
- The camera–IMU time offset differs between the recordings: td is −14.3 ms in recording 1 and −1.4 ms in recording 2, each ± 0.1 ms, while everything else repeats. The likely cause is the exposure time. The driver stamps each image a fixed 45 ms before it reaches the host in both bags, so the stamp follows the readout. td refers to the middle of the first row's exposure, which comes before the readout by half the exposure time: a longer exposure moves it earlier and makes td more negative.
- The bags don't record the exposure time. Measured from the motion blur, recording 1 was exposed for about 18 to 21 ms and recording 2 for about 2 to 5 ms. Half of that change is about 8 ms: the right direction, but short of the 13 ms measured, and the rest is still open. On the Dibuli Prism A4L, two exposures 1 ms apart moved td by 0.5 to 0.7 ms per ms of exposure, close to what this explanation predicts.
- In practice, td on this module depends on the exposure, so with auto-exposure it is not one number. Stamp frames at mid-exposure if the driver allows it, or use the td measured at an exposure close to yours; recording 2's value suits short exposures.

## How it was run

- Both cameras and the IMU, rolling shutter with each camera's readout time estimated, Kannala–Brandt (kb4) lenses with intrinsics free, IMU noise set about 5× tighter than MVIS's default to match this unit, t_ga estimated. Fast motion blurred some frames; stereo pairs whose board edges were more than 1.5× wider than the median were left out (17 % of the pairs in recording 1, 0.6 % in recording 2). The IMU stored accel 4× and gyro 2× too small; both were scaled before solving. Both recordings solved 2026-11-21 with MVIS 0.3.0, which reads the ChArUco board natively, with the same settings; cx and cy are about 0.45 px lower than in the first solves of 2026-11-14 and 2026-11-15.

# CyperStereo four-camera module camera–IMU calibration | OpenMVIS

URL: https://openmvis.com/devices/cyperstereo/

## Demo and values

Four-camera inertial module from Shenzhen Tujian Intelligent Technology (图间智能). Four global-shutter RGB cameras sit on separate 25 × 25 mm boards, cabled to one controller with a Bosch BMI088 IMU; two cameras have 160° lenses and two have 200° lenses, and the baseline is set by how the boards are mounted. One recording, solved as four cameras + IMU.
The 3D scene MVIS recovered from this recording, first 20 s, each camera in turn.

## Limits

- No independent reference, so these values show what MVIS solved, not how close they are to the truth.
- The board never reached the outer side of the two 200° images (about half of each image is covered), so the lens model there is extrapolated.
- IMU χ²/dof is 0.03 with the IMU noise set from the BMI088 datasheet, about 2.5× wider. A digital twin of this recording, with the noise exactly as set, gives about 0.06, so the setting is a little wider than the real noise, not far off.
- In the digital twin (6 noisy seeds) every value is recovered within tolerance except the four camera-to-IMU rotations: worst 3.0 mrad against 2 mrad, within 1.8× MVIS's own σ (1.7 mrad). The 39.5 s recording constrains rotation less than a longer one would.
- The tag size is taken from the target file sent with the data and isn't confirmed on the printed board. It scales every baseline and lever arm.

## How it was run

- All four cameras and the IMU together. Camera intrinsics (Kannala–Brandt kb4) from four single-camera solves of the same recording, then held fixed; IMU scale and misalignment, gyro-to-accel offset t_ga and camera time offsets estimated. IMU noise from the BMI088 datasheet, about 2.5× wider. Solved 2026-11-15.

## Limits

- No independent reference, so this shows consistency between the two solves, not accuracy.

URL: https://openmvis.com/devices/gi-ego1/

## Demo and values

Head-worn stereo headset from General Intelligence Labs with two colour rolling-shutter fisheye cameras and a 9-DoF IMU. One 30-second recording of an AprilGrid, solved with MVIS for camera, IMU and time offsets, with the rolling-shutter readout estimated too.

Reprojection median 0.15 px
cam0–cam1 baseline 62.1 mm
cam0 td, first row +55.55 ms +42.30 ms at mid-frame
cam0 lever arm 31.9 mm

Reprojection is how far, in pixels, the detected corners lie from where the solve puts them. td is the camera–IMU time offset, and the lever arm is the camera–IMU position offset.
One recording, with no independent reference. These values show what MVIS solved, not how close they are to the truth.

## Calibration process

The path of the rig around the board, as MVIS solved it. To explore it:

- Press Play or drag the bar to follow the path.
- Use the view buttons to change the view.
- Pick a camera card to put that camera on the frustum, the pyramid that shows its view.
Each card draws the board from the solved pose, with the corners MVIS detected. We publish no camera images.

## Limits

- No independent reference. These values show what MVIS solved, not how close they are to the truth.
- The supplier's IMU noise file (gyro 0.002, accel 0.02) is tuned for Kalibr, about 10× and 3× the noise measured at rest. Used as is in MVIS, it put unit A's lever arm 20 to 45 mm too far forward. These results use the measured noise with a 2 to 3× margin.
- With IMU intrinsics free, the lever arm's y shifts about 9 mm on both units, more than its 3.5 mm uncertainty. Pinned, it agrees with the supplier's Kalibr, so these results pin the IMU intrinsics.
- The listing says 1080P and 160°, and the supplier's sheet says 1920×1200 and 123.6°. These recordings are 1920×1200. The listing's shutter value wasn't tested here.

## How it was run

- cam0 at 30 Hz, cam1 at 10 Hz, t_ga estimated, camera intrinsics free, IMU intrinsics pinned. IMU noise padded from the measured noise: gyro 6e-4 rad/s/√Hz, accel 0.015 m/s²/√Hz. Batch of 2026-11-07.

# HP Reverb G2 camera–IMU calibration | OpenMVIS

URL: https://openmvis.com/devices/hp-reverb-g2/

## Demo and values

VR headset from HP with four 640×480 grayscale tracking cameras and an IMU at about 1 kHz. All four are solved from the Monado SLAM calibration data, in three pair recordings stitched together.
Recovered by MVIS from the Monado calibration data.

Reprojection median 0.13 px
cam0–cam1 baseline 108.5 mm
cam0 td −1.22 ms
cam0 lever arm 53.9 mm

Reprojection is how far, in pixels, the detected corners lie from where the solve puts them. td is the camera–IMU time offset, and the lever arm is the camera–IMU position offset.
Three pair recordings, with no independent reference on this page. These values show what MVIS solved, not how close they are to the truth.

## Calibration process

The path of the rig around the board, as MVIS solved it. To explore it:

- Press Play or drag the bar to follow the path.
- Use the view buttons to change the view.
- Pick a camera card to put that camera on the frustum, the pyramid that shows its view.
Each card draws the board from the solved pose, with the corners MVIS detected. We publish no camera images.

## Solved rig

The solved rig in 3D, to scale. Tap a sensor to see its values. In full screen you can rotate and zoom. Grid squares are 20 mm.

## Limits

- Three pair recordings, with no independent reference on this page. These values show what MVIS solved, not how close they are to the truth.
- This rig is stitched from three solves, not one joint solve. Cameras seen in two pairs agree to 0.89 mm and 0.34° (cam0) and 0.54 mm and 0.15° (cam1). cam2 and cam3 move 0.79 and 0.52 mm depending on how they are attached.
- The process figure and values for the IMU show the cam0 + cam1 recording only.

## How it was run

- Each recording shows the board to one camera pair, so three pairs are solved: cam0 + cam1, cam0 + cam2, cam1 + cam3. Each is camera + IMU with camera intrinsics free and t_ga estimated, on current MVIS, 2026-11-03. cam0, cam1 and all IMU values come from the first pair. cam2 is attached through cam0 and cam3 through cam1.

# Insta360 ONE RS 1-Inch 360 Edition camera–IMU calibration | OpenMVIS

URL: https://openmvis.com/devices/insta360-one-rs-1inch-360/

## Demo and values

Consumer 360° camera from Insta360 with two 1-inch sensors behind back-to-back fisheye lenses of about 200° each and a built-in IMU at 1 kHz. It is the camera of the Hilti-Trimble SLAM Challenge 2026 dataset. Each lens is solved with the IMU from the organisers' own calibration recording, using only the part where the camera turns about all three axes, with the rolling-shutter readout and the shape of the calibration board estimated. The first tab puts the two solves together as one rig.
The 3D scene MVIS recovered from the front-lens recording of the Hilti-Trimble SLAM Challenge 2026 (CC BY-NC-SA 3.0).

The time offsets, to scale. td is the camera–IMU time offset, with t_imu = t_cam + td. For a rolling-shutter camera td is the time of the first image row; the middle row is td + readout / 2, which is what a global-shutter calibration reports.

Board shape peak to peak 12.4 mm peak to peak 12.4 mm peak to peak 11.6 mm
The calibration board isn't perfectly flat, so this solve estimated the height of every corner off the flat board along with the calibration. The board's mean plane and tilt belong to its pose, so a flat board shows only noise here.

Lever z mm | +23.37 |
log(R) rad | [+1.2245, +1.1946, −1.2048] |
td ms | −20.962 |
Reprojection px | 0.393 |
Readout ms | +31.15 |
IMU |
t_ga ms | −0.06 ± 0.07 |

Parameter | MVIS |
cam0 |
fx px | 467.29 |
fy px | 466.58 |
cx px | 734.33 |
cy px | 719.46 |
alpha | 0.69400 |

Lever z mm | +20.56 |
