to cover every row of this table.

## The reasons, in equations

### Extrinsic rotation: two directions needed

The camera’s angular velocity (from its board poses) and the gyro’s are the same
vector in two frames:

${}^{I}\boldsymbol\omega(t) = {}^{I}_{C_i}\mathbf{R}\;{}^{C_i}\boldsymbol\omega(t) \quad\text{(after time alignment)}$
A rotation is fixed by two non-parallel vector pairs. If every
${}^{C_i}\boldsymbol\omega$ is parallel to one axis, any rotation about that axis
fits equally well. The start-value step of MVIS records the singular values of
the camera–gyro angular-velocity cross-covariance for this reason: one large and
two tiny ones mean one-axis rotation.

### Lever arm: only rotation shows it

The camera sits at ${}^{G}\mathbf{p}_{C} = {}^{G}\mathbf{p}_{I} + {}^{G}_{I}\mathbf{R}\,{}^{I}\mathbf{p}_{C}$.
Differentiate twice and compare with what the accelerometer measures:

${}^{G}\ddot{\mathbf{p}}_{C} = {}^{G}\ddot{\mathbf{p}}_{I} +
{}^{G}_{I}\mathbf{R}\Big(\big({}^{I}\dot{\boldsymbol\omega}\big)^\wedge + \big(({}^{I}\boldsymbol\omega)^\wedge\big)^2\Big)\,{}^{I}\mathbf{p}_{C}$

- No rotation: both terms vanish and ${}^{I}\mathbf{p}_{C}$ is a constant
offset the board pose absorbs.

- Rotation about one axis $\mathbf{k}$: a component of ${}^{I}\mathbf{p}_{C}$
along $\mathbf{k}$ gives $\mathbf{k}\times\mathbf{p} = 0$, so that component
stays unobservable.

The same holds for the lever arm of an auxiliary IMU.

### Time offset: a shift is seen through velocity

A time offset error $\delta t$ moves the pose used for a frame to a slightly
different time:

${}^{G}_{I}\mathbf{T}(t + \delta t) \approx {}^{G}_{I}\mathbf{T}(t)\;\mathrm{Exp}\!\left(\begin{bmatrix}{}^{I}\boldsymbol\omega\\ {}^{I}\mathbf{v}\end{bmatrix}\delta t\right)$

- At rest the shift changes nothing.

- At constant angular and linear velocity the shift is a constant relative
transform. The extrinsic absorbs it, and $t_{d,i}$ and the extrinsic cannot be
told apart.

- When the velocity changes the shift varies over the recording and no
constant transform can explain it. That is the signal.

### Readout: a shift per row

On a rolling-shutter camera, a corner on row $v_m$ is captured at
$t_C + t_{d,i} + \eta(v_m)\,t_{r,i}$. The readout is a time offset that grows from
the top row to the bottom row. It needs motion that moves the rows differently:
rotation about the camera’s x or y axis, which sweeps the image vertically or
horizontally. Rotation about the optical axis gives little signal, and so does a
board that covers only a few rows: then $t_{r,i}$ cannot be told from $t_{d,i}$.
See Why calibrate rolling shutter.

### IMU scale and misalignment: every axis excited

The corrected readings are
${}^{I}\boldsymbol\omega = {}^{I}_{w}\mathbf{R}\,\mathbf{D}_w(\boldsymbol\omega_m - \mathbf{b}_g - \mathbf{T}_g\,{}^{I}\mathbf{a})$
and ${}^{I}\mathbf{a} = {}^{I}_{a}\mathbf{R}\,\mathbf{D}_a(\mathbf{a}_m - \mathbf{b}_a)$
(Base IMU factor).
Column $n$ of $\mathbf{D}_w$ multiplies only axis $n$ of the reading. If that axis
never turns, the column has nothing to scale.

The accelerometer measures specific force, ${}^{I}\mathbf{a} = {}^{I}_{G}\mathbf{R}\,({}^{G}\ddot{\mathbf{p}}_I - {}^{G}\mathbf{g})$.
Gravity is about 9.8 m/s², far larger than hand-held acceleration. So tilting the
rig until each axis has pointed along gravity is what excites $\mathbf{D}_a$. A
rig held at one tilt sees one fixed gravity vector: then the scale and the bias
along it trade off against each other.

### G-sensitivity: acceleration must vary apart from rotation

$\mathbf{T}_g\,{}^{I}\mathbf{a}$ adds to the gyro reading. With mostly gravity in
${}^{I}\mathbf{a}$, its effect looks like a gyro bias that changes with tilt, which
the biases and $\mathbf{D}_w$ can also explain. It separates only with strong
linear acceleration on all axes. Hand-held motion rarely gives that, so it stays
pinned by default.

### t_ga: seen through the change in acceleration

The accelerometer reading that belongs to gyro time $t$ is the one stamped
$t + t_{ga}$. To first order:

$\mathbf{a}_m(t + t_{ga}) \approx \mathbf{a}_m(t) + t_{ga}\,\dot{\mathbf{a}}_m(t)$
The offset is visible only through $\dot{\mathbf{a}}_m$, the rate of change of
the specific force. Smooth, steady motion leaves it loose; brisk reversals make it
sharp. The response of some IMUs also depends on the frequency of the motion, so
one value can be a compromise: see Why calibrate t_ga.

## How much signal is enough

Observable is not yes or no in practice. A value can be observable in theory and
still weak on a given recording: the 1σ then comes out wide, and the value moves
from one recording to the next. Two ways to check:

- Read the 1σ next to each value in the result. Compare it across recordings.

- Run the digital twin of your own rig and motion: MVIS simulates the
recording with known truth and solves it (step 7).

What happens when a motion is missing, and how MVIS reports it:
Degeneracy.

## What this means for your recording

- Rotate about all three axes, at varied speed, with the board in view.

- Tilt the rig through many orientations, so gravity falls along every axis.

- Change direction briskly a few times. Avoid long stretches of steady motion.

- Sweep the board across all image rows, more so for a rolling-shutter camera.

- Hold still for about 3 s at both ends. The rests give the motion a clean
start and end; the start-value step can compare a still start with its
gyro-bias estimate.


---

# Degeneracy | OpenMVIS

URL: https://openmvis.com/concepts/degeneracy/

Use this page when a calibration value looks wrong or varies between
recordings, and you suspect the motion.

A motion is degenerate for a value when it gives the data no way to measure
that value (Observability explains the reasons). A
degenerate value does not make the solve fail. It converges, the residuals look
fine, and the value sits near its start or drifts with noise. So you have to look
for it.

Symbols follow Notation & glossary.

## Degenerate motions

Motion | What is lost | How it shows |
Pure translation (no rotation) | lever arm (all 3 axes); gyro scale $\mathbf{D}_w$; the extrinsic rotation is fixed only by the direction of gravity and acceleration, so it is weak; readout and time offset are weak | lever stays near its start with a wide 1σ; $\mathbf{D}_w$ diagonal stays near 1 |
Rotation about one axis only | the lever-arm component along that axis; extrinsic rotation about that axis; $\mathbf{D}_w$ columns of the other two axes; readout, if the axis is the optical axis | one lever component with a much wider 1σ than the others; the rotation-excitation check shows one large singular value and two tiny ones |
Constant velocity (steady turning and moving) | time offset $t_{d,i}$ (a time shift looks like a fixed transform); t_ga (no change in acceleration); $\mathbf{D}_a$ gets no signal beyond the gravity tilts | $t_{d,i}$ and the lever move together between recordings |
Planar motion (rig slides in a plane and turns only about its normal, as on a cart or a table) | everything one-axis rotation loses; with a vertical normal, gravity stays on one IMU axis, so the other $\mathbf{D}_a$ columns and the accel bias along gravity trade off | as one-axis rotation, plus $\mathbf{D}_a$ diagonals with a wide 1σ |
Too slow | time offset, readout and t_ga (all need fast change); weak $\mathbf{D}_w$ | wide 1σ on the timing values; readout far from the sensor’s spec |
Too short | fewer distinct orientations; biases and IMU scales separate poorly | values move a lot between recordings |
Board always centred, face-on | lens distortion and focal length | distortion differs between recordings; residuals grow toward the image edges |

$\mathbf{T}_g$ is weak under almost any hand-held motion. That is why it is pinned
unless you set estimate.imu.intrinsics: full.

## How MVIS shows it

MVIS does not stop a run because the motion was weak. It reports, at four points.

### Before the solve

- Recording length: mvis inspect warns when a recording with an IMU is
shorter than 30 s.

- Window choice: for bags longer than 80 s, the camera–IMU run keeps the 80 s
with the most gyro and accelerometer excitation, scored per IMU as the mean
squared angular rate plus the variance of the acceleration magnitude
(input.window_mode: motion).

### In the start values

The start-value step runs simple fits before the joint solve and checks them:

- Rotation excitation: the singular values of the camera–gyro angular-velocity
fit. One large and two tiny ones mean rotation about one axis.

- Time-offset sharpness: how much the fit error rises away from the best
offset. A flat minimum means the offset is weak.

- Lever arm: if its 1σ in the linear fit is over 5 cm, it starts at 0.

- Accelerometer bias: it starts at 0. The start step estimates it only when
asked (an advanced start option); it then falls back to 0 when the linear fit
cannot separate it (smallest singular value of the scaled system under 10⁻³, or
1σ over 0.05 m/s²).

- Gravity and scale: the fitted gravity should be close to 9.81 m/s² and the
scale within 3 % of 1. A miss points at wrong intrinsics, units or stamps.

- Auxiliary IMUs: the gyro-to-gyro start needs a clear minimum (1.5 times
sharper than the edges) and more than 10 s of overlap.

A value that starts at 0 is still solved jointly; the start only keeps a poor
guess out.

### In the joint solve

Freed IMU intrinsics carry a weak prior (0.1 on $\mathbf{D}_w$ and
$\mathbf{D}_a$). On a direction the motion does not excite, that prior wins: the
value stays near its start instead of wandering. Its 1σ then stays close to the
prior’s 0.1: that is the sign the motion did not excite it.

### In the results

- 1σ for every value: from the marginal covariance of the joint solve, in the
result JSON and the report. Compare each with the others of its kind and across
recordings.

- Camera-only report, motion grades: each camera gets a grade (good,
marginal, poor) per value, from its board poses. The thresholds are empirical:

Grade for | Measure | Good | Marginal |
focal length | farthest over nearest board distance | over 2.0 | over 1.5 |
distortion | image area covered by the board corners | over 60 % | over 30 % |
rotation diversity | smallest over largest spread of the rotation axes | over 0.1 | over 0.03 |
time offset | spread of the angular speed | over 0.5 rad/s | over 0.2 rad/s |
readout | peak angular speed about the camera’s x and y axes | over 1.0 rad/s | over 0.3 rad/s |

- Camera–IMU report, motion and excitation: the angular velocity of the
solved trajectory over time. Gaps and one-axis stretches are easy to see.

- mvis verdict: grades a result green, yellow or red. It flags a χ² per
degree of freedom (the weighted squared error divided by its degrees of
freedom, about 1 when the noise model fits) over 1.5 (yellow) or 3.0 (red), a solve that hit its
iteration cap, an IMU scale more than 5 % from 1, and a camera time offset over
50 ms. A wrong value from weak motion can still pass these; the 1σ and a second
recording are the stronger checks.

## Check it yourself

- Calibrate two or more recordings. A value that moves far more than its 1σ
between them was not observed.

- Run the digital twin. MVIS replays your motion on a simulated copy of your
rig with known truth, solves it, and shows which values come back
(step 7: digital-twin check).

- Run the round trip. Correct the data with the result and calibrate again;
if the first result was right, the second finds nothing left to correct
(step 8: round-trip validation).

## What to do

If you see | Add to the motion |
lever arm weak, or one component weak | rotation about the other axes, with brisk changes of turning speed |
$t_{d,i}$ moves between recordings | changes of speed and direction; avoid long steady sweeps |
readout weak or off | faster tilts about the camera’s x and y axes, board across all rows |
t_ga weak | short, sharp reversals |
$\mathbf{D}_a$ weak | tilt the rig so each axis points up and down at some point |
$\mathbf{D}_w$ weak | turns about every axis, at several speeds |
distortion differs | move the board into the image corners and edges |

The motion in step 2: record the dataset covers all
of these in about 60 s. Its motions that fail
list the same cases from the recording side.


---

# Configuration | OpenMVIS

URL: https://openmvis.com/reference/configuration/

Use this page to look up any key in an MVIS config file.
One YAML file describes the board, the inputs and the solve.
There are two config types:

- Camera-only (mode: cam): calibrates the cameras alone.

- Camera–IMU (mode: cam-imu): adds one or more IMUs (inertial measurement units:
gyroscope and accelerometer) to a camera rig.

mvis run reads mode: to pick the pipeline; mvis cam and mvis cam-imu ignore it.
For the commands, see the CLI reference.

Checked against MVIS 0.1.0
We wrote this page by hand from the MVIS 0.1.0 config code.
Run mvis check -c config.yaml to lint a file: the solver only logs an unknown key and goes on,
check reports it.

## Rules for every config

- Paths: ${VAR} expands to the environment variable and a leading ~ to your home folder.
${MVIS_DATASETS} defaults to a Datasets folder in your home directory.

- Units: lengths in metres, times in seconds, angles in radians, unless a key says otherwise.

- Unknown keys: logged as a warning and ignored.

- Aliases: target_hz is read as factor_hz; sigma_px and pixel_sigma are read as each other;
pin_tr: true is read as estimate_readout: false.

- Camera models: radtan, equidistant, kb4, fov, double_sphere, eucm, ucm,
omni_radtan (experimental). fisheye and kannala_brandt mean kb4 (why).
See Camera model.

## board

The calibration target. Both config types use the same block.

Key | Default | For | Meaning |
board_type | chessboard | all | apriltag (AprilGrid), chessboard or aruco |
rows, cols | 9, 6 | all | Tag rows and columns; inner corners for a chessboard |
tag_size | 0.02 | apriltag | Tag edge length (m) |
tag_spacing | 0.005 | apriltag | Gap between tags. Below 1 it is a fraction of tag_size (Kalibr’s convention); 1 or more is metres |
tag_family | t36h11 | apriltag | AprilTag family |
square_size | 0.025 | chessboard | Square edge length (m) |
marker_size | 0.02 | aruco | Marker edge length (m) |
marker_separation | 0.005 | aruco | Gap between markers (m) |
aruco_dict | DICT_6X6_250 | aruco | OpenCV dictionary name |
heights_file | none | camera–IMU | Start values for the board shape: one height per corner. The <output>_board_shape.yaml of an earlier camera–IMU run is a valid file. Camera-only runs do not read it |

board.detection holds expert settings for the multi-scale AprilTag detector.
The defaults suit most boards; leave it out unless detection misses tags.

## estimate

The estimate: block says what is solved and what is held fixed.
Both config types read it.
It wins over the older low-level keys it maps to (the parser warns when both are set).
Leave a key out to keep the default.

estimate :

camera : # every camera; a camera entry can override with its own estimate:

intrinsics : true # focal length and principal point

distortion : true # distortion coefficients

tr : false # rolling-shutter readout

td : true # time offset

extrinsics : true # camera pose in the rig

imu : # every IMU (camera–IMU only)

intrinsics : dw_da # how much IMU intrinsics to solve

model : calyx # which IMU model: kalibr | rpng | calyx

extrinsics : true # auxiliary IMU pose in the base IMU frame

td : true # auxiliary IMU time offset to the base IMU

board_points : false # board shape: one height per corner

Key | Default | Camera-only | Camera–IMU |
camera.intrinsics | true | Solve the intrinsics | Refine the prior intrinsics; false pins them to camera_input.path |
camera.distortion | true | Not read: the solver always estimates distortion | Follows camera.intrinsics |
camera.tr | false | Not read: set shutter_type: rolling on the camera | Solve the readout of rolling-shutter cameras |
camera.td | camera-only false, camera–IMU true | Camera–camera time offsets (unsynchronised cameras) | Camera to base-IMU time offset |
camera.extrinsics | true | Not read: always estimated | Solve T_CtoI |
imu.intrinsics | dw_da | — | pinned, dw_da (scale and misalignment), dw_da_r (plus the gyro-to-accelerometer rotation), full (plus Tg); true = full, false = pinned |
imu.model | calyx | — | kalibr, rpng or calyx: a convention, see IMU model |
imu.extrinsics | true | — | Solve each auxiliary IMU’s pose in the base IMU frame |
imu.td | true | — | Solve each auxiliary IMU’s time offset |
board_points | false | Solve one height per board corner | Same; one board only |

A false on a camera–IMU key adds a very tight prior that holds the value at its start.
Board heights carry a weak 3 mm prior (solve.board_height_sigma on camera–IMU).
Their mean and the two tilts are held at zero, so the board pose keeps the plane.

VI-Rig: estimate the board shape
The VI-Rig AprilGrid is not flat. Set estimate.board_points: true in every VI-Rig
config, camera-only and camera–IMU. Other boards keep the default unless you measured them
non-flat. See Board shape.

## Camera-only config

Two shapes are accepted. They mean the same thing.

Flat shape | Sectioned shape |
cameras: | input.cameras: |
— | input.cache_dir: |
optimizer: | solve: |
output_file: | output.path: |
output_format: | output.format: |

board:, estimate:, report: and the top-level keys are the same in both.
mvis calibrate reads only the flat shape.

### cameras[]

One entry per camera, under cameras: or input.cameras:.

Key | Default | Meaning |
camera_id | 0 | Camera index; reference_camera refers to it |
name | empty | Label in reports |
source_type | images | images, timestamped_images, rosbag_topic (ROS1 bag), ros2bag or euroc |
source_path | empty | Image folder, ROS1 bag file, ROS2 bag folder (or one .db3 / .mcap file) or EuRoC camera folder. For timestamped_images: image_dir,timestamps.csv |
topic | empty | Image topic; required for bag sources |
distortion_model | radtan | Camera model; models may differ between cameras of one rig |
shutter_type | auto | global, rolling or auto (treated as global). rolling estimates the readout |
factor_hz | solve.factor_hz | Frames per second used in the solve |
initial_intrinsics | none | Start values [fx, fy, cx, cy], instead of the automatic first guess |
initial_distortion | none | Start values for the distortion coefficients |
estimate | none | Per-camera override of estimate.camera |

Bag topics can be sensor_msgs/Image or PNG or JPEG sensor_msgs/CompressedImage.
JPEG is lossy and can move corners, so MVIS warns once per topic.
There is no video input: extract frames to an image folder first.

### optimizer / solve

Key | Default | Meaning |
max_iterations | 200 | Levenberg–Marquardt (LM) iterations of the joint solve |
max_init_frames | 100 | Frames used for the first guess; 0 = no cap |
init_frame_selection | uniform | uniform (spaced in time) or diverse (spread over position, size and tilt) |
factor_hz | 5.0 | Frame rate for cameras without their own factor_hz |
pixel_sigma | 1.0 | Corner noise (px) |
huber_threshold | 1.345 | Huber robust-loss threshold |
optimize_intrinsics | true | Older form of estimate.camera.intrinsics |
pnp_method | iterative | First-guess pose solver: iterative or ippe (planar) |
lm_lambda_lower, lm_lambda_upper | 0, 100 | LM damping bounds |

Four nested groups hold expert settings. Their defaults suit most rigs:

- frame_quality: detection gates, for example min_tags_per_frame: 6, min_corner_views: 5,
max_pnp_reprojection_px: 10.

- trajectory_alignment: first guess of extrinsics and time offsets, for example max_expected_dt_s: 0.5.

- outlier_rejection: the second pass, for example enabled: true, threshold_px: 2.0, percentile: 99.

- guardrail: when to fall back to the first pass, for example p95_regression_factor: 1.5.

### Top-level keys

Key | Default | Meaning |
mode | cam | cam or cam-imu; read by mvis run |
reference_camera | 0 | Camera the extrinsics are expressed in |
corner_subsample | two_anti | Corners kept per AprilGrid tag. See below |
optimize_time_offset | false | Solve camera–camera time offsets; for unsynchronised cameras |
rerun_outliers | true | Run a second pass without outliers; it falls back to the first pass if the second one goes wrong |
rerun_visualization | false | Open the Rerun 3D viewer (needs the viz extra) |
output_file | calibration_result.yaml | Result path (flat shape) |
output_format | yaml | yaml or json (flat shape) |
report.thumbnail_max_dim | 320 | Size of detection thumbnails in the report (px) |

corner_subsample values:

- two_anti (camera-only default): two diagonal corners per tag. Faster than all, and in our runs
on VI-Rig and TUM-VI (MVIS 0.1.0) the principal point stayed within about 0.1 px of it.

- two_diag: the other diagonal pair.

- all (camera–IMU default): every corner.

- top_left, top_right, bottom_left, bottom_right (or tl, tr, bl, br): one corner per tag.
Fastest, but in the same runs it moved cx and cy by up to about 0.8 px, and reprojection error does not show it.

With few tags it falls back to all. The first guess always uses every corner.
The sectioned shape also accepts solve.corner_subsample; the top-level key wins.

### Example: VI-Rig cameras

The three cameras of the VI-Rig 4 IMUs + 3 cams set.

virig_3cams_cam.yaml
mode : cam

input :

cameras :

- camera_id : 0

name : Blackfly

source_type : rosbag_topic

source_path : ${MVIS_DATASETS}/mvis_4imus_3cams/virig_4imus_3cams_april_01.bag

topic : /blackfly/image_raw

distortion_model : radtan

shutter_type : global

factor_hz : 15.0

- camera_id : 1

name : T265-1

source_type : rosbag_topic

source_path : ${MVIS_DATASETS}/mvis_4imus_3cams/virig_4imus_3cams_april_01.bag

topic : /t265/fisheye1/image_raw

distortion_model : kb4

shutter_type : global

factor_hz : 15.0

- camera_id : 2

name : T265-2

source_type : rosbag_topic

source_path : ${MVIS_DATASETS}/mvis_4imus_3cams/virig_4imus_3cams_april_01.bag

topic : /t265/fisheye2/image_raw

distortion_model : kb4

shutter_type : global

factor_hz : 15.0

board : { board_type : apriltag , rows : 6 , cols : 6 , tag_size : 0.088 , tag_spacing : 0.3 , tag_family : t36h11 }

solve :

max_iterations : 15 # enough for this board; default 200

output :

path : results/virig_3cams/calibration.yaml

reference_camera : 0

optimize_time_offset : true

estimate :

board_points : true

## Camera–IMU config

Top-level sections: input, board, camera_input, solve, estimate, output and
the optional reference, plus the gravity keys.
Camera–IMU calibration is two steps:

- Calibrate the cameras (camera-only config).

- Give that result to camera_input.path and solve with the IMUs.

### input

Key | Default | Meaning |
format | ros1 | ros1 (ROS1 bag), ros2 (ROS2 bag folder, or one .db3 / .mcap file) or euroc (EuRoC / ASL mav0 folder) |
path | empty | ROS1 bag file, ROS2 bag folder or .db3 / .mcap file, or mav0 folder |
bags | empty | Several recordings: each is calibrated into its own bag<NN>/cam_imu.json next to output.path. Each inherits format |
cam_topics | from camera_input.path | Image topics, in camera order. Empty = the topics stored in the camera calibration |
imu_topics | ["/imu0"] | IMU topics. The first is the base IMU; the rest are auxiliary IMUs |
imus | empty | Per-IMU options, in imu_topics order. {gyro_only: true} calibrates an auxiliary IMU from its gyroscope alone; not allowed on the base IMU |
window_mode | motion | motion picks the segment_length seconds with the most IMU motion; manual uses t0 and window |
segment_length | 80.0 | Window length in motion mode (s). A shorter recording falls back to manual |
t0 | 3.0 | Window start in manual mode (s from the start) |
window | 0.0 | Window length in manual mode (s); 0 = to the end |
min_obs | 4 | Fewest board corners for a frame to be kept |
cache_dir | none | Folder for the detection cache (capture database); none = no cache |

ROS1, ROS2 and EuRoC all feed camera–IMU runs. apply-calib and roundtrip read ROS1 bags only.

### camera_input

Key | Default | Meaning |
path | empty | Camera calibration: a _calib.yaml from mvis cam, or a Kalibr camchain |
free_intrinsics | true | Refine the camera intrinsics with the IMU. Older form of estimate.camera.intrinsics |
estimate_readout | false | Solve the rolling-shutter readout. Older form of estimate.camera.tr |
rolling_mode | 0 | Which row the frame stamp refers to: 0 top, 1 middle, 2 bottom |
cameras | empty | Per-camera overrides, in camera order. See below |

camera_input.cameras[i] accepts free_intrinsics, estimate_readout, rolling_mode,
factor_hz (vision factors per second for that camera) and vision_pose (imu or interp).
For cameras whose stamps are not on the sensor clock, retime_sensor_clock: true
solves a per-frame capture offset first, and retime_map reuses the <output>_sensor_clock.json
of an earlier run.

### solve

Three terms first:

- td: the camera–IMU time offset.

- t_ga: the time offset between the gyroscope and accelerometer of one IMU (why).

- State: the IMU pose, velocity and biases at one instant; states are placed at state_hz.

Key | Default | Meaning |
state_hz | 30.0 | Rate of the states (Hz); 0 = one per base-camera frame |
factor_hz | 10.0 | Vision factors (frames used) per second per camera |
max_iterations | 50 | LM iterations |
sigma_px | 1.0 | Corner noise (px) |
huber_px | 2.0 | Huber threshold (px); 0 turns the robust loss off |
corner_subsample | all | Corners kept per tag; values as in camera-only |
vision_pose | imu | How a frame’s pose is found between two states: imu propagates the IMU samples to the capture time; interp interpolates between the two states |
imu_intrinsics | dw_da | Older form of estimate.imu.intrinsics |
imu_intrinsics_model | calyx | Older form of estimate.imu.model |
estimate_t_ga | true | Solve t_ga for the base IMU and every auxiliary IMU that is not gyro_only |
sigma_t_ga | 0.010 | Prior on t_ga (s) |
estimate_readout | false | Solve the rolling-shutter readout for every camera |
board_height_sigma | 0.003 | Prior on each board-corner height (m), with estimate.board_points: true |
sigma_td_prior | 0.0 | Prior that holds each camera’s td near its start (s); 0 = off |
pnp_method | iterative | First-guess pose solver: iterative or ippe (planar) |
rms_gate_px | 0.0 | Mark the result ok: false when the final reprojection RMS is above this; 0 = off |
init_kwargs | {} | Options for the camera–IMU first guess, for example keyframe_hz (default 2.0) and scale_rel_tol (default 0.10) |

IMU noise, as continuous-time densities:

Key | Default | Meaning |
sigma_g | 0.01 | Gyroscope noise (rad/s/√Hz) |
sigma_bg | 0.001 | Gyroscope bias random walk (rad/s²/√Hz) |
sigma_a | 0.02 | Accelerometer noise (m/s²/√Hz) |
sigma_ba | 0.002 | Accelerometer bias random walk (m/s³/√Hz) |

Set them from your IMU’s measured noise densities (for example an Allan-variance fit),
inflated two to three times. The values in a Kalibr imu.yaml are not drop-in values for these keys.

Multi-IMU and expert keys:

Key | Default | Meaning |
aux_imu_stride | 3 | One auxiliary-IMU factor per this many base-IMU state intervals. A larger stride means fewer factors and a faster solve; the auxiliary levers move a little with it |
aux_imu_factor_hz | 0.0 | Rate of auxiliary-IMU factors (Hz). Used only when aux_imu_stride is 0; with both 0, one factor per base interval |
imu_min_rate_hz | 200.0 | An IMU slower than this is upsampled before integration; 0 = off |
imu_upsample_method | cubic | linear or cubic |
sigma_dw_da, sigma_tg, sigma_imu_R | 0.1, 0.05, 0.1 | Weak priors on the free IMU intrinsics |
sigma_v0, sigma_bg0, sigma_ba0 | 0.5, 0.01, 0.1 | Priors on the first state’s velocity and biases |
bound_intrinsics | false | Keep free camera intrinsics in their valid range (for example double_sphere ξ in [−1, 1]) |
vision_imu_linearized | true | With vision_pose: imu, the reprojection factor integrates the IMU once and corrects linearly, like the IMU factor; it integrates again only when t_ga or td moves far. false integrates at every evaluation |
tga_relin_threshold_s | 0.003 | Integrate an IMU’s factors again when its t_ga has moved more than this (s) from where they were integrated; 0 = never |
max_interp_dt | 0.3 | Frames between states further apart than this (s) are dropped |
lm_lambda_lower, lm_lambda_upper | 0, 100 | LM damping bounds |

### Gravity: gravity and site

Top-level keys, from MVIS 0.4.0. Set the gravity where the data was recorded: the
accelerometer scale takes up any error in the gravity magnitude
(Local gravity has the calculator).

gravity : 9.8013 # m/s², Newark, Delaware

Key | Default | Meaning |
gravity | none | Gravity in m/s², local or measured. Also accepted as solve.gravity. Must be between 9.70 and 9.90 |
site | none | {latitude_deg, longitude_deg, altitude_m, name}: where the data was recorded. MVIS computes WGS84 normal gravity from it, and the report names the place. altitude_m defaults to 0; longitude_deg and name are for display only |

- Neither: 9.81 m/s², and the run log warns.

- Both: they must agree to 0.01 m/s², else the config is rejected.

- The place in the report: from MVIS 0.4.1 the comment after the gravity: value names it;
with site: the report names the site.

- The value used and its source (default, config or site) are in cam_imu.json
(gravity_mps2, gravity_source), the calibration YAML and the report.

### output

Key | Default | Meaning |
path | cam_imu_calib.json | Summary JSON. The other files are named after it |
calib_yaml | <path>_calib.yaml | Full MVIS calibration, the input of apply-calib |
kalibr_yaml | <path>_camchain-imucam.yaml | Kalibr camchain-imucam export |
report_html | <path>_report.html | HTML report |
report_txt | none | Text report |

See Result formats.

### reference

Known values to compare against: CAD, factory or published numbers.
The HTML report and mvis verdict -c read it. It is a consistency check, not ground truth.

Key | Meaning |
label | Name shown in the report, for example factory |
lever_mm | Per camera (cam0: or 0:): the camera position in the base IMU frame, [x, y, z] in mm |
baseline_mm | Stereo baseline between cam0 and cam1 in mm: a length or a 3-vector |

### Example: VI-Rig cameras + 4 IMUs

All three cameras and four IMUs of the
VI-Rig 4 IMUs + 3 cams set, with the camera result of the
example above as the prior.

virig_3cams_cam_imu.yaml
gravity : 9.8013 # m/s², Newark, Delaware

mode : cam-imu

input :

format : ros1

path : ${MVIS_DATASETS}/mvis_4imus_3cams/virig_4imus_3cams_april_01.bag

cam_topics :

- /blackfly/image_raw

- /t265/fisheye1/image_raw

- /t265/fisheye2/image_raw

imu_topics :

- /imu/data # base IMU

- /gx3_25/data # auxiliary IMUs

- /gx3_35/imu/data

- /t265/imu

window_mode : motion

segment_length : 80.0

cache_dir : results/virig_3cams/cache

board : { board_type : apriltag , rows : 6 , cols : 6 , tag_size : 0.088 , tag_spacing : 0.3 , tag_family : t36h11 }

camera_input :

path : results/virig_3cams/calibration.yaml

cameras :

- {}

- factor_hz : 4.0

- factor_hz : 4.0

solve :

max_iterations : 40 # as in our VI-Rig runs; default 50

estimate :

board_points : true

camera : { intrinsics : true , tr : false , td : true , extrinsics : true }

imu : { intrinsics : dw_da , model : calyx , extrinsics : true , td : true }

output :

path : results/virig_3cams/cam_imu.json

More configs ship under examples/configs/ in the
repository:

- tga_mvis/: VI-Rig camera–IMU runs, one per base IMU

- tumvi_cam_imu/: TUM-VI camera–IMU, one config per camera model (see its README)

- example_cam_run.yaml, example_estimate.yaml: commented camera-only and camera–IMU templates

- recalib_example.yaml: an apply-calib config


---

# CLI | OpenMVIS

URL: https://openmvis.com/reference/cli/

Use this page to look up every mvis subcommand and its flags.
MVIS installs one command, mvis, with ten subcommands.

- Flags choose what to run and where the output goes.

- The YAML config says how to calibrate. Its keys are on
Configuration.

mvis --help # list the subcommands

mvis --version # print the MVIS version

mvis cam-imu --help # flags of one subcommand

Checked against MVIS 0.1.0
We wrote this page by hand and checked it against the --help output of MVIS 0.1.0.
If the two disagree, mvis <subcommand> --help is right.

Subcommand | What it does |
run | Calibrate from any config; the config’s mode: picks camera-only or camera–IMU |
cam | Camera-only calibration |
cam-imu | Joint camera–IMU calibration |
calibrate | Older camera-only path for flat configs |
apply-calib | Apply a camera–IMU calibration to a raw ROS1 bag and write a corrected bag |
roundtrip | Calibrate, apply, recalibrate and report PASS or FAIL |
check | Check the installation and lint a config before a solve |
inspect | Summarise a recording: format, streams, rates, overlap |
verdict | Grade a finished result GREEN, YELLOW or RED |
datasets | List, download and verify the benchmark datasets |

## A typical session

mvis inspect recording.bag # can MVIS read it, and which modes?

mvis check -c config.yaml # is the config valid, are the extras installed?

mvis run -c config.yaml # calibrate

mvis verdict result.json # grade the result

## Exit codes

Subcommand | 0 | 1 | 2 |
check, inspect | pass | warn | fail |
verdict | GREEN | YELLOW | RED |
roundtrip | PASS | FAIL | invalid config or arguments |
datasets | every file OK | a file is missing or fails its check | invalid arguments |
cam, run (mode: cam) | solved | the solve failed | invalid arguments |

cam and cam-imu exit 3 when the stored result does not match the files they wrote.
That is an internal consistency check; please report it as a bug.

cam-imu prints its summary JSON whether or not the solve succeeded.
Read ok in that JSON, or grade it with verdict.

## run

Calibrate from one config file.
The top-level mode: key picks the pipeline:

- mode: cam (the default when mode: is absent): runs cam.

- mode: cam-imu: runs cam-imu and prints its summary JSON.

mvis run -c config.yaml

Flag | Default | Meaning |
-c, --config | required | Run config YAML |

## cam

Camera-only calibration: intrinsics, distortion, extrinsics between cameras,
camera–camera time offsets and rolling-shutter readout.
It reads both config shapes, the flat one and the sectioned one
(see Camera-only config).

mvis cam -c t265/cam.yaml

mvis cam -c t265/cam.yaml -o results/run # writes results/run/t265_cam_calib.yaml

Flag | Default | Meaning |
-c, --config | required | Camera-only config YAML |
-o, --output | <output_file folder>/ablation | Run folder for the report, log and detection cache. By default a folder named ablation next to output_file |

The run folder is cleared before the solve, except its caches.
MVIS clears only a folder it created; it refuses any other folder that already exists.
The run folder holds <name>_calib.yaml, <name>_full.yaml, <name>.html,
<name>.log and detections.mvisdb.
<name> is <config folder>_<config file name>.
The result is also written to the config’s output_file.
See Result formats.

## cam-imu

Joint camera–IMU calibration. It estimates:

- Extrinsics: T_CtoI, the pose of each camera in the base IMU frame.
The base IMU is the first entry of input.imu_topics.

- Time offset td: between each camera clock and the base IMU clock.

- Rolling-shutter readout: when estimate.camera.tr is on.

- Camera intrinsics: when estimate.camera.intrinsics is on.

- IMU intrinsics: gyro and accelerometer scale and misalignment (Dw, Da), optional Tg.

- Biases: gyro and accelerometer.

- t_ga: the gyro-to-accelerometer time offset, for the base IMU and every auxiliary IMU that is not gyro_only (why).

- Auxiliary IMUs: extrinsics, time offset and intrinsics of every further IMU.

mvis cam-imu -c cam_imu.yaml

mvis cam-imu -c cam_imu.yaml --bag other_recording.bag

Flag | Default | Meaning |
-c, --config | required | Camera–IMU config YAML |
--bag | from config | Use this ROS1 bag instead of the config’s input. Sets input.format: ros1 and input.path to the bag |

With input.bags the config calibrates many recordings in one call.
Each one gets its own bag<NN>/cam_imu.json next to output.path.
The command prints a JSON summary of the run.
See Camera–IMU calibration.

## calibrate

The older camera-only path. It reads the flat config shape only and does not
write the run folder, report or capture database that mvis cam writes.
Use cam or run for new work.

mvis calibrate -c config.yaml

Flag | Default | Meaning |
-c, --config | required | Flat camera-only config YAML |

## apply-calib

Apply a saved camera–IMU calibration to a raw ROS1 bag.
It writes a corrected bag and a provenance file, <output bag>.recalib.yaml, that
records the calibration, the topic mapping and which corrections ran.
By default it applies every correction, in this order
(details):

- t_ga: re-samples the accelerometer at t + t_ga, when t_ga was calibrated.

- IMU intrinsics: applies the inverse IMU model (Dw, Da, Tg) to every IMU.

- Bias: subtracts the calibrated static gyro and accelerometer bias, inside the same inverse model.

- td: re-stamps every camera and auxiliary IMU message onto the base IMU clock, using the header stamp.

mvis apply-calib -c recalib.yaml

mvis apply-calib --calib cam_imu_calib.yaml --in raw.bag --out corrected.bag

mvis apply-calib --calib cam_imu_calib.yaml --in raw.bag --no-td --keep-bias

Flag | Default | Meaning |
-c, --config | — | Config YAML with calib, input, output and the switches below. Flags override it |
--calib | config calib | Calibration to apply: the _calib.yaml that mvis cam-imu writes |
--in | config input | Raw input ROS1 bag |
--out | <input>.corrected.bag | Output bag. An existing bag is not overwritten |
--map | derived | YAML {base_imu_topic, mapping: {topic: sensor}}. Rarely needed: the calibration stores each sensor’s topic |
--keep-bias | off | Keep the static IMU biases (config remove_bias: false) |
--no-imu-intrinsics | off | Skip the inverse IMU model; remove only the bias (config imu_intrinsics: false) |
--no-t-ga | off | Skip the accelerometer t_ga re-sampling (config t_ga: false) |
--no-td | off | Keep the original header and record stamps (config td: false) |
--undistort | off | Also undistort mono8 images (config undistort: true) |
--strict | off | Stop with an error instead of passing data through (config strict: true). See below |

--strict rejects:

- mapped topics that are missing or empty

- messages of the wrong type

- images it cannot undistort

- duplicate IMU stamps on a topic that gets the t_ga correction

- corrected IMU values that are not finite

The bag is streamed, so memory does not grow with its size.
Rolling-shutter rows are not unwarped; only the frame stamp moves.
More in Round-trip validation, section “Export a corrected dataset”.

## roundtrip

End-to-end check of a camera–IMU calibration on a ROS1 bag:

- Calibrate the bag.

- Apply the calibration to the same bag.

- Calibrate the corrected bag.

- Compare the two results and report PASS or FAIL.

On the corrected bag, IMU intrinsics must move to identity and biases to zero,
while extrinsics and the stereo baseline must stay the same.
A remaining td is reported as a warning only.

mvis roundtrip -c cam_imu.yaml

Flag | Default | Meaning |
-c, --config | required | Camera–IMU config YAML for a ROS1 bag |
--out | results/roundtrip/<name> | Output folder: forward/cam_imu.json, recal/cam_imu.json, report.txt (readable), report.json |
--bag | from config | Round-trip this ROS1 bag instead of the config’s input |
--keep-corrected | off | Keep the corrected bag; it is deleted by default |
--keep-bias | off | Pass --keep-bias to apply-calib |

It exits 1 on FAIL, so it works as a CI gate.
What PASS means: Round-trip validation.

## check

Check the installation and lint a config before a solve.
The solver accepts configs leniently and only logs unknown keys; check is strict.
Each finding has a stable id and a status pass, warn or fail.

mvis check # check the installation

mvis check --env --smoke # also run a short synthetic camera solve

mvis check -c config.yaml # lint a config

mvis check -c config.yaml --env --json

Flag | Default | Meaning |
-c, --config | — | Run config YAML to lint |
--env | on when no -c | Check the installation; with -c, also the optional extras that config needs (AprilGrid, ArUco, ROS bags) |
--smoke | off | Also run a short synthetic camera solve. Implies --env |
--json | off | Print JSON {status, findings} |
--out | — | Also write the JSON findings to this file |

## inspect

Summarise a recording before you calibrate it.
It reads only metadata and a short sample of each stream.
It reports:

- the container format and which modes can read it (cam, cam-imu)

- camera streams: rate, resolution, encoding

- IMU streams: rate, unit sanity, stamp order

- the time overlap of cameras and IMUs

- a warning when a recording with IMUs is shorter than 30 s, because a camera–IMU run needs at least 30 s of motion

mvis inspect recording.bag

mvis inspect dataset/mav0 --json

Argument | Default | Meaning |
path | required | ROS1 bag, ROS2 bag folder (or one .db3 / .mcap file), EuRoC mav0 folder or image folder |
--json | off | Machine-readable output |
--out | — | Also write the JSON report to this file |

ROS1 bags, ROS2 bags and EuRoC folders can feed both modes; image folders feed camera-only.
apply-calib and roundtrip need a ROS1 bag.

## verdict

Grade a finished result.
Each check has a stable id, the measured value, its threshold and a status.
The grade is RED if any check fails, YELLOW if any warns, GREEN otherwise.
The checks cover:

- reprojection error: median, P95, RMS

- physical plausibility: focal aspect ratio, principal point, finite distortion

- data: corner observations per camera

- camera–IMU solves: solver status, iterations, td, IMU fit, IMU scale

- with -c: lever arm and stereo baseline against the config’s reference: block

mvis verdict results/run/t265_cam_calib.yaml

mvis verdict cam_imu.json -c cam_imu.yaml --independent-check roundtrip

Argument | Default | Meaning |
result | required | Camera-only result YAML or camera–IMU summary JSON |
-c, --config | — | Camera–IMU config whose reference: block is compared |
--independent-check | none | Independent check you already ran: none, roundtrip, holdout, repeatability, cross-tool. Recorded in the verdict |
--json | off | Print JSON |
--out | — | Also write the JSON verdict to this file |

verdict never takes a solver’s ok: true as proof of a good fit; see Evaluation & metrics.

## datasets

The catalog of benchmark datasets on Hugging Face
(calibench-vi/datasets).
Files go to $MVIS_DATASETS, by default a Datasets folder in your home directory.
The shipped example configs refer to them as ${MVIS_DATASETS}/....

The VI-Rig sets are gated: accept the terms on the Hub page, then set
HF_TOKEN to a read token (or run hf auth login, after pip install huggingface_hub) before you download.

See Datasets.

mvis datasets list

mvis datasets list --dataset mvis_4imus_3cams

mvis datasets download --select mvis_4imus_3cams/april_01 # about 7 GB

mvis datasets download --selection smoke

mvis datasets verify --dataset mvis_4imus_3cams

mvis_4imus_3cams is the catalog key of VI-Rig 4 IMUs + 3 cams.

Action | What it does |
list | Print each dataset with its licence, and each sequence with its size and URL |
download | Download and checksum the chosen sequences |
verify | Check the local files’ sizes and checksums |
convert | Convert a third-party dataset from its native format to ROS1 bags |
export-recipes | Write stand-alone conversion scripts for datasets that cannot be re-hosted |
upload | Maintainers only: push converted bags to the Hub |

Flag | Default | Meaning |
--dataset | all | One dataset key, for example mvis_4imus_3cams |
--select | — | DATASET or DATASET/SEQUENCE; repeat it to pick several |
--selection | — | A built-in selection (smoke: one sequence from each of eight datasets, VI-Rig april_01 first) or a JSON file {dataset: [sequences]} |
--suite | all | Only the sequences of one test suite: camera-only or camera-imu |
--allow-unverified | off | download: also fetch files the catalog has no checksum for |
--mcap | off | convert: also write a ROS2 MCAP copy of each bag |
--out | recipes | export-recipes: output folder |
--dry-run | off | upload: print the plan only |

## Environment variables

Variable | Default | Meaning |
MVIS_DATASETS | Datasets in your home directory | Where mvis datasets puts files; ${MVIS_DATASETS} in configs expands to it |
MVIS_BLAS_THREADS | 1 | BLAS threads for the process. 0 keeps the library default. An exported OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS, OMP_NUM_THREADS or MKL_NUM_THREADS is never overridden |
MVIS_EIGEN_CACHE_CPU | lowest allowed CPU | CPU whose cache sizes the linear algebra uses, so a solve does not depend on which core it starts on. off reads them wherever the first product runs |

The mvis command uses one BLAS thread because the solvers run many small matrix
products in Python. Extra threads only spin, and results can change with the thread count.
import mvis as a library leaves these settings alone.

## Scripts in the repository

These ship in the source repository, not as subcommands:

Script | What it does |
scripts/setup_env.sh | One-step conda setup; see Installation |
scripts/test.sh <tier> | Run the tests by tier: unit, solver, integration or full; extra arguments go to pytest |
scripts/visualize_result.py <run_dir> | Post-hoc Rerun 3D viewer for a result directory (--no-spawn to attach to a running viewer) |
scripts/run_calibration.py | Multi-camera ablation: calibrate with each camera as the reference |
scripts/recalib_batch.py | Apply one calibration across every *.bag in a directory (--calib, --in-dir, --out-dir) |
python -m mvis.analysis.regenerate_html [root] | Rebuild HTML reports from saved YAML + detection cache |

The maintainers’ regression runner and its baselines are not part of the public
repository; Regression testing describes
that workflow.

More detail in Evaluation & metrics.


---

# Result formats | OpenMVIS

URL: https://openmvis.com/reference/result-formats/

Use this page to see what a run writes and which file to use for what.

Run | Files | Use for |
mvis cam | <name>_calib.yaml, <name>_full.yaml, <name>.html, <name>.log | Deploy the _calib.yaml; keep the rest to reproduce the run |
mvis cam-imu | cam_imu.json, cam_imu_calib.yaml, cam_imu_camchain-imucam.yaml, cam_imu_report.html | Read the JSON; deploy or apply the _calib.yaml; give Kalibr users the camchain |
mvis apply-calib | <bag>.corrected.bag, <bag>.corrected.bag.recalib.yaml | The corrected recording and how it was made |
mvis roundtrip | forward/, recal/, report.txt, report.json | PASS or FAIL with every check |

Rotations are stored as matrices (3×3 or 4×4) or log(R) rotation vectors in radians,
never roll, pitch and yaw. Board tilt against gravity is the one angle given in degrees.

## Camera-only results

mvis cam writes into the run folder (-o; by default a folder named ablation next to output_file).
<name> is <config folder>_<config file name>: -c t265/cam.yaml gives t265_cam_calib.yaml.

File | Contains | Use for |
<name>_calib.yaml | Intrinsics, distortion, extrinsics, time offsets, readout, reprojection statistics | Deploy. The calibration itself |
<name>_full.yaml | The above, plus per-frame board poses, board corners, timings, filter statistics, motion metrics | Replay. Rebuild the report or the 3D view without detecting again |
<name>.html | The report | Read it first; see below |
<name>.log | The run log | Debugging |
detections.mvisdb | Detections and this run’s estimates | See Capture database |

With rerun_outliers: true, the first pass is kept as <name>_pass1_calib.yaml,
<name>_pass1_full.yaml and <name>_pass1.html when it differs from the final result.
The config’s output_file gets a copy of the result, in YAML or JSON (output_format).

### Fields of the camera-only _calib.yaml

Field | Meaning |
cameras[] | Per camera: id, model (pinhole_<distortion model>), intrinsics (fx, fy, cx, cy), distortion (model, coeffs), image_size, rolling_shutter_readout (s) |
cameras[].rolling_shutter_readout_sigma | Formal 1σ of the readout (s), when it was estimated |
cameras[].valid_domain | kb4 only: the largest angle the fit can project, up to the model’s first fold |
extrinsics | reference_camera and transforms[]: from, to, T_to_from (4×4), so3 (log(R), rad), translation (m) |
time_offsets | reference_camera and offsets[]: camera, dt (s) |
reprojection_errors | overall_rms and per_camera[]: rms, mean, median, p90, p95, max (px), num_observations |
board_shape | With estimate.board_points: true: heights_m per corner, rms_mm, peak_to_peak_mm, n_obs |
board_point_bias | Mean residual per board corner: median_px, max_px, n_points_seen |
corner_accounting | What became of every detected corner; see below |

## Camera–IMU results

mvis cam-imu names every file after output.path.
With output.path: results/run/cam_imu.json:

File | Contains | Use for |
cam_imu.json | A compact summary in practical units (mm, ms) | Read, compare, grade with mvis verdict |
cam_imu_calib.yaml | The full calibration in SI units, with each sensor’s topic | Deploy, and the input of mvis apply-calib |
cam_imu_camchain-imucam.yaml | Kalibr camchain-imucam | Tools that read Kalibr files |
cam_imu_report.html | The report | Read it first |
cam_imu_views.json | The report’s 3D scene and rig views, without camera frames | Rebuild the 3D views elsewhere, for example on openmvis.com |
cam_imu_board_shape.yaml | The estimated board shape, with estimate.board_points: true | board.heights_file of a later run |
cam_imu_sensor_clock.json | Per-frame stamp maps, with retime_sensor_clock | camera_input.cameras[i].retime_map of a later run |

### Fields of cam_imu.json

Field | Meaning |
ok | The solve finished and passed its own gates. Not proof of a good fit |
reproj_rms_px, reproj_median_px, reproj_p95_px | Reprojection error over all cameras (px) |
solve_s | Solve time (s) |
diagnostics | iterations, max_iterations, cam_chi2_dof, imu_chi2_dof, n_states |
cams[] | Per camera: td_ms, reproj, reproj_median, reproj_p95 (px), intr, p_CinI_mm (camera position in the base IMU frame), rotvec (log(R) of T_CtoI, rad), p_CtoC0_mm (position relative to camera 0), corner_accounting |
imu_model | kalibr, rpng or calyx |
Dw_diag, Da_diag | Diagonals of the base IMU’s gyroscope and accelerometer matrices |
Dw_scale, Dw_shear, gyro_misalign_rotvec | calyx only: Dw split into a rotation (log(R), rad) and an upper-triangular part with the scales on its diagonal |
t_ga_ms, t_ga_sigma_ms | Base IMU gyro-to-accelerometer time offset and its 1σ (ms) |
gravity_mps2, gravity_source | The gravity the solve used (m/s²) and where it came from: default (9.81, neither gravity: nor site: in the config), config (gravity:) or site (WGS84 normal gravity at site:) |
gravity_site | With site: in the config: name, latitude_deg, longitude_deg, altitude_m and g_site, the normal gravity there (m/s²). The report names it |
init_gates | Checks on the initial guess, not on the solve: g_norm_ls (the gravity norm the unconstrained initial fit found, m/s²), g_norm_ok, scale (the board-to-motion scale of that fit), scale_ok (within 3 % of 1). A failed gate is a warning; ok does not use them |
imus[] | Per auxiliary IMU: td_ms, t_ga_ms, chi2_dof, p_IsinI_mm (position in the base IMU frame), rotvec, Dw_diag, Da_diag |
board | Board pose against gravity: T_BinW, g_inB, normal_tilt_deg, g_inplane_deg; shape with estimate.board_points: true |

td convention: an image stamped t matches the IMU at t + td.

### Fields of the camera–IMU _calib.yaml

Field | Meaning |
cameras[] | As in the camera-only file, plus td (s), T_cam_imu (4×4, IMU to camera), reproj_rms_px, p_CtoC0_m, rostopic |
imus[] | First the base IMU (role: base), then each auxiliary IMU (role: aux) |
imus[].b_g, imus[].b_a | Gyroscope (rad/s) and accelerometer (m/s²) bias |
imus[].Dw, imus[].Da | 3×3 gyroscope and accelerometer matrices, in the convention of model |
imus[].imu_intr_xi | Every IMU intrinsic in one vector, including Tg and the internal rotation; the form apply-calib reads |
imus[].R_wtoI, imus[].U_w | Base IMU, calyx: rotation and upper-triangular factor of Dw |
imus[].t_ga, imus[].t_ga_sigma | Gyro-to-accelerometer time offset and its 1σ (s), when estimated |
imus[].td, imus[].p_IsinI_m | Auxiliary IMU: time offset (s) and position in the base IMU frame (m) |
imus[].gyro_only | Present and true when an auxiliary IMU was calibrated from its gyroscope alone; its lever, Da and accelerometer bias were held fixed |
imus[].topic | Source topic; apply-calib uses it to map topics to sensors |

IMU intrinsics depend on the convention
Dw and Da compare only between calibrations with the same imu.model.
Check the model before you compare numbers. See IMU model.

### Several recordings

With input.bags, each recording gets its own folder next to output.path:

results/sweep/

bag01/cam_imu.json

bag02/cam_imu.json

bag03/cam_imu.json

<NN> is the last number in the bag file name (for a EuRoC mav0 folder, the first number of its parent folder).

## Corner accounting

Every result has a corner_accounting block per camera.
It says what happened to each detected corner, so a fit cannot look better by silently dropping corners.
Every corner lands in exactly one category:
detected = used + past_fold + other_invalid + outliers + no_pose_corners + not_in_solve.

Field | Meaning |
detected | Every corner given to the solve |
used | Had a factor in the final solve and projects at the final fit |
past_fold | Fails to project at the final fit, at or past a Kannala–Brandt model’s fold |
other_invalid | Fails to project for another reason, for example behind the camera under equidistant |
outliers | Removed by the outlier filter; still projects |
no_pose_frames, no_pose_corners | Frames, and their corners, that reached no factor (no pose, too few points) |
not_in_solve | Never reached the final solve: thinned by rate or corner_subsample, or dropped by a gate |
past_fold_pass1 | past_fold at the first pass’s fit, before the outlier rerun. Above zero also raises the alarm |
n_corners | used + past_fold + other_invalid |
max_theta_deg, max_theta_used_deg | Largest angle from the optical axis, of all corners and of the used ones |
fold_deg, fold_level | kb4: angle of the fold. fold_level is alarm when corners lie past the fold, warn when the fold lies inside the image, else none |

## HTML reports

Every run writes one self-contained HTML file. It has no external files, so you can mail it.
It prints cleanly and has a dark mode.

The camera-only report has:

- Summary: stat cards and a table of contents

- Intrinsics and distortion: tables per camera

- Extrinsics: a table and a 3D plot

- Temporal calibration: time offsets and readout

- Reprojection: per-frame median and P95, per tag, error-vector histograms, corner heatmaps

- Data quality: motion-excitation grades, rotation-axis spread, angular-velocity timeline, image coverage

- Detection statistics, pipeline timing and collapsible appendices

The camera–IMU report adds:

- Summary: status, reprojection RMS, χ²/dof, with grade badges

- 3D views: the sensor rig (each camera at its T_CtoI, each auxiliary IMU, levers in mm)
and the recovered trajectory with the board

- Cameras, base IMU, auxiliary IMUs: every estimate, with its 1σ where the solve gives one

- Against reference: lever, rotation and baseline differences, when the config has a reference: block

The reprojection and χ²/dof badges use the same thresholds as mvis verdict. See Evaluation & metrics.

To rebuild a camera-only report from a finished run folder without solving again:

python -m mvis.analysis.regenerate_html results/run --config t265/cam.yaml

## Corrected bags

mvis apply-calib writes an ordinary ROS1 bag.
Anything that read the raw bag reads the corrected one.
Next to it, <bag>.recalib.yaml records:

- the source bag and the calibration file, with its SHA-256

- the base IMU topic and the timeline (base_imu_clock, or the original stamps with --no-td)

- the td convention: t_on_base = t_sensor + td

- which corrections ran: remove_bias, undistort, imu_intrinsics, td, t_ga

- which topics were corrected and which were copied unchanged

## Kalibr files

mvis.io.kalibr reads and writes Kalibr files; its functions are listed in
Python API.
A Kalibr calibration can be an MVIS start (camera_input.path takes a camchain),
and an MVIS result can go to tools that expect Kalibr.
Notes on the exported camchain-imucam:

- kb4: written as Kalibr pinhole + equidistant with the same coefficients.
Exact for points in front of the camera; MVIS warns when the fit used corners past 90°.

- Readout: written as Kalibr’s line_delay, the readout divided by the image rows.

- rostopic: written as /camN/image_raw; set your own topics before you use the file with Kalibr.

- Skipped export: when a camera cannot be expressed in Kalibr’s form (for example ucm with α outside [0, 1)),
the camchain is not written and MVIS logs a warning. The MVIS files still hold the full result.


---

# Python API | OpenMVIS

URL: https://openmvis.com/reference/python-api/

Use this page to find which MVIS module to import for each job.
MVIS is a Python library: the mvis command is a thin layer over the functions below.
The package is pymvis; you import it as mvis.

import mvis

print ( mvis.__version__ ) # 0.1.0

A map, not generated docs
We wrote this page by hand from the MVIS 0.1.0 source.
The docstrings in the repository hold the full signatures.
MVIS 0.x releases may change the Python API and the config schema; the
changelog lists what changed.

## Package layout

Module | Contents |
mvis.core | Result types (Observation, CameraParams, CalibrationResult), the config dataclasses, timing |
mvis.camera | One CameraModel class per camera model: projection, Jacobians and unprojection in one place |
mvis.detection | Boards (chessboard, AprilGrid, ArUco), detectors, frame quality, corner subsampling |
mvis.io | Data sources, the streaming detection pipeline, image decoding, the camera–IMU loader, output writers, Kalibr and Basalt files |
mvis.imu | IMU intrinsic models (kalibr, rpng, calyx), resampling, Allan-variance analysis |
mvis.calibration | First guess, factor graph, camera-only and camera–IMU pipelines, outlier rejection |
mvis.simulation | Synthetic camera–IMU data, digital twins, simulator examples |
mvis.recalib | apply-calib and roundtrip |
mvis.datasets | The dataset catalog behind mvis datasets |
mvis.doctor | mvis check and mvis inspect |
mvis.mvisdb | The capture database |
mvis.analysis | HTML reports, plots, the Rerun 3D view, motion analysis, verdict |
mvis.cli | The mvis command |

Terms:

- Jacobian: the derivatives of a projection with respect to its inputs; the solver needs them.

- Unprojection: the reverse of projection, from a pixel back to a viewing ray.

- First guess: OpenCV’s pose-from-known-points solve (PnP) and a focal-length estimate, before the joint solve.

## Load and check a config

from mvis.core.config import CamRunConfig, CamImuRunConfig, CalibrationConfig

from mvis.core.config_validator import validate_config

cam_cfg = CamRunConfig. from_yaml ( " t265/cam.yaml " ) # camera-only, flat or sectioned

imu_cfg = CamImuRunConfig. from_yaml ( " cam_imu.yaml " ) # camera–IMU

problems = validate_config ( CalibrationConfig. from_yaml ( " t265/cam.yaml " )) # list of strings

The fields are those on Configuration.
from_yaml expands ${MVIS_DATASETS} and ~, and warns on unknown keys.

## Run a calibration

Function | Does |
mvis.calibration.cam_run.run_cam(config_path, output=None, *, result_file=None, ...) | Camera-only run, as mvis cam; the other keyword arguments mirror its options. Returns 0 on success, 1 when the solve failed; raises SystemExit(3) on an internal consistency failure |
mvis.cli.main.calibrate_cam_imu(config) | Camera–IMU run from a CamImuRunConfig, as mvis cam-imu. Writes every output file and returns the summary dict (the cam_imu.json content) |
mvis.cli.main.calibrate_cam_imu_batch(config, out_dir) | One calibrate_cam_imu per entry of input.bags; returns {bag<NN>: summary} |
mvis.calibration.pipeline_cam_imu.run_cam_imu_calibration_multi(cams, board_points, t_imu, w_m, a_m, *, aux_imus=None, config=None) | The camera–IMU solve on arrays already in memory, without files. The simulator examples use it |

from mvis.core.config import CamImuRunConfig

from mvis.cli.main import calibrate_cam_imu

summary = calibrate_cam_imu ( CamImuRunConfig. from_yaml ( " cam_imu.yaml " ))

print ( summary [ " ok " ] , summary [ " cams " ] [ 0 ][ " p_CinI_mm " ], summary. get ( " t_ga_ms " ))

## Grade and inspect

Function | Does |
mvis.analysis.verdict.assess(path, reference=None) | Grade a result file, as mvis verdict. Returns a Verdict with grade and checks; .to_dict() for JSON |
mvis.doctor.inspect.inspect(path) | Summarise a recording, as mvis inspect. Returns a report with status, streams and findings |
mvis.doctor.check_config.check_env(needs=None, smoke=False) | Installation checks, as mvis check --env; a list of findings |
mvis.doctor.check_config.check_config(path) | Config lint, as mvis check -c; a list of findings |

Each finding has a stable id, a subject, a status (pass, warn, fail) and a message.

## Correct a bag and round-trip

Function | Does |
mvis.recalib.load_rig_calib(path) | Read a camera–IMU _calib.yaml for apply_calibration |
mvis.recalib.sensor_map.resolve_mapping(rig, map_path, cfg) | Topic-to-sensor mapping: a --map file, the config’s mapping:, or derived from the topics in the calibration |
mvis.recalib.apply.apply_calibration(in_bag, out_bag, rig, mapping, base_imu_topic, *, remove_bias=True, undistort=False, imu_intrinsics=True, td=True, t_ga=True, strict=False) | Write the corrected bag and its .recalib.yaml, as mvis apply-calib. Returns message counts and output paths |
mvis.recalib.roundtrip.run_roundtrip(config_path, *, out=None, keep_corrected=False, keep_bias=False, bag_override=None) | The whole round trip, as mvis roundtrip. Returns {ok, checks} |
mvis.recalib.roundtrip.roundtrip_report(forward, recal) | Compare two cam_imu.json dicts with the round-trip tolerances |

## Kalibr files

mvis.io.kalibr is the one place for Kalibr files.

Function | Does |
read_camchain(doc) | A Kalibr camchain dict → per-camera intrinsics, distortion, resolution |
read_camchain_imucam(doc) | Also each camera’s T_cam_imu and the stereo T_cn_cnm1 |
write_camchain_imucam(result) | A camera–IMU result → a camchain-imucam dict, ready for yaml.safe_dump |
parse_results(path), camera_only(dir), camera_imu(dir) | Read the output files of a finished Kalibr run |

A camchain is Kalibr’s YAML file of camera parameters.
T_cam_imu maps points from the IMU frame into the camera frame.
T_cn_cnm1 maps points from the previous camera into this one.

Kalibr AprilGrid target files load with
mvis.detection.apriltag_board.AprilTagBoard.from_kalibr_yaml(path).
Any board: config block builds a board with mvis.detection.board_factory.create_board(BoardConfig).

## Camera and IMU models

import numpy as np

from mvis.camera import create_camera_model

from mvis.imu import create_imu_model, KalibrImu, RpngImu, CalyxImu

cam = create_camera_model ( " kb4 " , fx = 286.7 , fy = 286.7 , cx = 415.0 , cy = 404.5 ,

distortion_coeffs = np. array ( [ - 0.005 , 0.036 , - 0.035 , 0.006 ] ))

- mvis.camera: PinholeRadtan, PinholeEquidistant, KannalaBrandt4, FOVModel,
DoubleSphere, EUCM, UCM, OmniRadtan. Each projects, unprojects and gives Jacobians.

- mvis.imu: the three IMU intrinsic models and their correction matrices
(dw_matrix, da_matrix, tg_matrix). See IMU model.

## Simulation

Simulator examples: a real recorded motion with a full rig setup, ready to simulate.

from mvis.simulation.examples import available, load_example, simulate

from mvis.calibration.pipeline_cam_imu import run_cam_imu_calibration_multi

print ( available ()) # example names

ex = load_example ( " twin_gs " )

data = simulate ( ex , seed = 0 ) # cams, t_imu, w_m, a_m, aux_imus

result = run_cam_imu_calibration_multi ( data [ " cams " ] , ex.board_points_flat , data [ " t_imu " ] ,

data [ " w_m " ] , data [ " a_m " ] ,

aux_imus = data [ " aux_imus " ] or None )

The installed package ships twin_gs. A source checkout also has the others under data/sim_examples/,
led by virig_4imus_3cams.
Their true values are real solves moved by a fixed, seeded perturbation, so no real device calibration ships.

Digital twins of whole recordings are in mvis.simulation.twin:
capture(config_path, name) builds a twin from a config and its recording,
Twin.load(path) reads a saved one, and solve(twin) simulates, runs the real solver
and returns the errors against the truth.
See Digital-twin check.

## Datasets and the capture database

from mvis.datasets import DatasetCatalog

cat = DatasetCatalog. load ()

ds = cat. get ( " mvis_4imus_3cams " )

print ( ds.license , [ s.sequence for s in ds. sequences () ] )

from mvis.mvisdb.manager import DatabaseManager

db = DatabaseManager ()

print ( db. runs ( " results/run/detections.mvisdb " )) # the runs stored in one capture

capture = db. load ( " results/run/detections.mvisdb " , run_id = 1 ) # an MVISDatabase with that run folded in

See Capture database.

## Reports

from mvis.analysis.cam_imu_report import write_cam_imu_report

write_cam_imu_report ( result , html_path = " report.html " , text_path = " report.txt " ,

reference = ref , board = board )

board and reference are optional; without board the report has no board in the 3D scene.
To rebuild a camera-only report from a finished run folder:
python -m mvis.analysis.regenerate_html <run folder> --config <config>.

## Why the models live in one place

A report cannot disagree with the fit it describes:
it computes residuals with the same code the solver minimised.

- mvis.camera holds each model’s projection, Jacobian and unprojection together.

- mvis.calibration.factors.camera_projection is shared by the solver and the HTML report.


---

# The capture database | OpenMVIS

URL: https://openmvis.com/reference/database/

Use this page to understand the .mvisdb file behind every MVIS run:
what it holds, where it lives and how to read it.

A .mvisdb file is one SQLite database per recording. It has two parts:

- Capture core: the expensive data, board detections and the full IMU streams.
It is written once and then sealed with a hash of its contents.

- Run overlay: one per run (run_id), written by each solve.
It records what the run used, why it left the rest out, and every estimate.

What this gives you:

- Detection runs once. A second solve of the same frames with the same board reuses the sealed core, whatever its solve settings.

- Deleting a run deletes its whole overlay and leaves the core alone.

- Every result can say why. Each frame, board pose and corner the solve left out carries an
exclude_reason and the stage that excluded it.

## Where it lives

Run | File |
mvis cam | detections.mvisdb in the run folder (-o). Clearing the run folder keeps it |
mvis cam-imu | One file per recording in input.cache_dir. Without cache_dir there is no cache |

The cache is keyed on the recording (source, topics or folders, time window) and the board
definition, including the detector settings. Two runs that read different topics or windows of
one bag never share an entry.

New detector code needs a fresh cache
The key does not include the MVIS version. If you update MVIS and want to compare detection,
delete the cache first; otherwise the new version reuses the old detections.

## Read it from Python

from mvis.mvisdb.manager import DatabaseManager

db = DatabaseManager ()

path = " results/run/detections.mvisdb "

print ( db. capture_info ( path )) # name and hashes of the recording

print ( db. runs ( path )) # the runs stored, oldest first

capture = db. load ( path , run_id = db. latest_solved_run_id ( path ))

print ( len ( capture.streams ) , " cameras, " , len ( capture.imus ) , " IMUs " )

load returns one MVISDatabase with that run’s overlay folded into the objects,
so pipeline code never sees SQL.
Any SQLite client can also open the file directly.

## The object model

This is the in-memory structure. There is one MVISDatabase per recording,
with one run’s overlay folded in as flags.

How to read the diagram:

- Notes are on the right.

- ⟨derived⟩ fields are computed, never stored.

- PK marks the primary key, the field that identifies each entry.

- Amber field names are the run’s flags and results, stored in the overlay.

MVISDatabase one capture: a live run, or one read back with DatabaseManager().load(path, run_id)
├─ streams: list[CameraStream] PK camera_id — the number you wrote in the YAML
│ ├─ camera_id · topic · source_type · source_path
│ ├─ info: CameraInfo
│ │ name · shutter · readout_s · rolling_mode
│ │ intrinsics · distortion · camera_model · resolution · calib_provenance
│ │ ⟨derived⟩ stereo_pair · projection · distortion_kind · is_fisheye
│ └─ frames: list[FrameData] PK frame_id · UNIQUE (camera_id, timestamp)
│ ├─ frame_id · camera_id · timestamp
│ ├─ is_motion_still · is_selected_to_use
│ ├─ ⟨derived⟩ is_valid_to_use = OR over every group below
│ └─ board_detections: list[BoardDetection] ONE PER BOARD SEEN · PK (frame_id, board_id)
│ ├─ board_id
│ ├─ ⟨derived⟩ n_detections · n_tags · detect_status
│ ├─ pose_cam_to_board: PoseCamToBoard{T, source} · is_valid_to_use
│ ├─ ⟨derived⟩ is_selected_to_use = frame.selected AND own selection
│ └─ detections: list[TagDetection] PK (frame_id, board_id, point_id)
│ ├─ point_id · uv · detector_emission_order
│ ├─ ⟨derived⟩ tag_id · corner_id · row = int(uv[1])
│ ├─ is_valid · is_selected · exclude_reason
│ └─ residual: Residual{residual_px, ⟨derived⟩ residual_source}
├─ boards: dict[int, Board] Board = {BoardInfo, [BoardPt]}
│ ├─ info: BoardInfo board_type · rows · cols · cell_size_m · gap_m · tag_family · start_id · corners_per_tag · config_hash
│ │ ⟨derived⟩ is_kalibr_tag · num_tags · num_points
│ └─ board_pts: list[BoardPt] board_pt_id · board_pt_3d · info: BoardPtInfo{tag_id, corner_id}
├─ imus: list[ImuStream] PK imu_id — the position in imu_topics
│ ├─ info: ImuInfo name · topic · frequency_hz · gyro_unit · accel_unit · gyro_only
│ │ gyro_noise · gyro_bias_noise · accel_noise · accel_bias_noise
│ │ intrinsics: ImuIntrinsics{xi24, model} · td_gyro_to_accel_s · calib_provenance ⟨derived⟩ role
│ └─ meas: ImuMeasurements t_gyro · gyro · t_accel · accel ⟨derived⟩ synchronized
├─ rig: Rig base_camera_id · base_imu_id · sync_kind · sync_tolerance_s
│ ⟨derived, per run⟩ reference_stream = (imu, base_imu_id) if cam_imu else (cam, base_camera_id)
├─ estimate_states: EstimateStates | None this run’s estimates, read from the run overlay
│ reference_stream: (cam, base_camera_id) | (imu, base_imu_id) the stream the states follow: camera in camera-only runs, base IMU in camera–IMU runs
│ state_hz rate of the states (Hz)
│ base_state: CamOnly{t, T_cam_to_board (F,7)} | CamImu{t, T_imu_to_world (K,7), v, b_g, b_a}
│ sensor_states[]: SensorState one per sensor — reference included (its factor_hz, relative = None)
│ sensor · factor_hz · relative{T_x_to_ref · td_x_to_ref_s · provenance}
│ · intrinsics: Camera{fxfycxcy · dist · model · readout · provenance} | Imu{xi24 · model · provenance}
│ boards[board_id]: T_board_to_world (7,) one per board — camera–IMU only
│ world_frame the gravity-aligned world frame; none in camera-only runs, where the board is the reference
└─ run_id: int | None every run field above resolves against this

## On-disk form

The same structure is stored in four groups of tables:

Group | Tables | Notes |
Meta | schema_meta | Schema version and when the file was created |
Capture core | capture, camera, imu / imu_meas, board / board_pt, rig, stereo_pair, and the observations frame → board_detection → detection | Corner and IMU arrays are packed float64 blobs. Sealed once capture.content_hash is set |
Run overlay (per run_id) | run; the selection: frame_status, board_detection_status, detection_status; the results: result_camera, result_imu, extrinsic | The selection tables store only rows that differ from “selected and valid”. extrinsic holds every camera–camera, camera–IMU and IMU–IMU transform with its T, time offset and sigmas |
Trajectory (camera–IMU runs) | estimate_meta, state_knot / state_var, frame_bracket, world_frame | state_knot / state_var: the state timeline and its variables. frame_bracket: which two states bracket each frame, and where. world_frame: the gravity-aligned world |

Every overlay table uses ON DELETE CASCADE: deleting a run row deletes all of its overlay rows.

The status tables mirror the core tables one for one.
That keeps two things cheap: recording each selection decision as it is made,
and checking the stored flags against the data the solve used.


---

# Evaluation & metrics | OpenMVIS

URL: https://openmvis.com/reference/evaluation/

Use this page to tell whether a calibration is good.
Check it in this order:

- Read the report: did the motion exercise every parameter?

- Run mvis verdict: are the fit and the values plausible?

- Run an independent check: round trip, repeatability, another tool or a digital twin.

The same metrics back the leaderboard, so a local run and a
published entry measure the same thing.

## 1. Read the report first

Every run writes a self-contained HTML report (what is in it).
Read its data quality section before the error numbers. It shows:

- Motion excitation: grades for how much the motion moved each axis

- Rotation-axis spread: whether you rotated about all three axes

- Angular-velocity timeline: where in the recording the motion was

- Image coverage: where the board corners fell in each image

Reprojection error is not accuracy
Reprojection error is the pixel distance between the detected and the predicted board corners.
It says how well the result explains the data it was fitted to.
A parameter the motion never excited stays near its start value without raising the error.
A low error on a poorly excited recording means little.

## 2. Grade it with mvis verdict

mvis verdict results/run/t265_cam_calib.yaml # camera-only

mvis verdict results/run/cam_imu.json -c cam_imu.yaml # camera–IMU, with its reference: block

Each check is pass, warn or fail.
The grade is RED if any check fails, YELLOW if any warns, GREEN otherwise.
The camera–IMU HTML report uses the same thresholds for its badges.

Check | id | Pass | Warn | Fail |
Reprojection median | reproj.median | ≤ 1.41 px | ≤ 2.83 px | above |
Reprojection P95 | reproj.p95 | ≤ 2.83 px | ≤ 5.66 px | above |
Reprojection RMS (when no median) | reproj.rms | ≤ 1.41 px | ≤ 2.83 px | above |
Camera and IMU fit, χ²/dof | fit.cam_chi2_dof, fit.imu_chi2_dof, fit.aux_imu_chi2_dof | ≤ 1.5 | ≤ 3.0 | above |
Focal length | intr.focal_positive | fx, fy > 0 | — | otherwise |
Focal aspect | intr.focal_aspect | |fx/fy − 1| ≤ 0.02 | above | — |
Principal point | intr.principal_point | within 10 % of the image size from the centre | further | — |
Distortion | intr.distortion_finite | finite | — | not finite |
Reprojection present | reproj.missing | every camera has errors | — | a camera has none |
Cameras in the result | result.cameras | at least one | — | none |
Corner observations per camera (camera-only) | data.observations | ≥ 500 | fewer | — |
IMU scale (camera–IMU) | imu.dw_scale, imu.da_scale | |diagonal − 1| ≤ 0.05 | above | — |
Camera–IMU time offset | time.td | |td| ≤ 50 ms | above | — |
Solver status | solve.ok | true | — | false |
Iterations | solve.converged | below max_iterations | hit the cap | — |
Solver step | solve.lm_step | took at least one step | took no step | took no step and failed |
Lever against reference: | ref.lever | ≤ 10 mm | above | — |
Baseline against reference: | ref.baseline | ≤ 5 mm | above | — |

Notes:

- Pixel units: the reprojection thresholds are on the length of each corner’s 2D error,
as Kalibr reports it. They are per-axis limits times √2: 1 and 2 px for the median and RMS, 2 and 4 px for the P95.

- χ²/dof: the solve’s cost per degree of freedom. Near 1 means the noise settings match the data.

- Warnings can be real: a raw consumer IMU can have a scale error above 5 %, and a USB camera
a td above 50 ms. Confirm them across recordings.

- ok: true from the solver only means it finished and passed its own gates. verdict never
counts it as proof of a good fit.

## 3. Check it independently

mvis verdict --independent-check <kind> records which check you ran: roundtrip, holdout, repeatability or cross-tool (another tool). A digital twin has no kind of its own.

### Round trip

mvis roundtrip -c cam_imu.yaml

It needs no ground truth.
MVIS applies the calibration to its own bag and calibrates the corrected bag again.
PASS needs every one of these on the corrected bag:

Quantity | Expected after correction | Tolerance |
Dw, Da diagonals | 1 | within 0.01 |
Gyroscope and accelerometer bias | 0 | below 0.02 (rad/s, m/s²) |
Lever and stereo baseline | unchanged | within 2 mm |
td | 0 | above 2 ms is a warning only, because td can be weakly observable |

The IMU terms must collapse to identity and zero while the geometry stays the same.
See Round-trip validation.

### Repeatability

Calibrate several recordings of one rig with input.bags and compare the results.
A parameter that moves between recordings was not pinned down by the motion in them.
See Camera–IMU calibration.

### Hold-out recording

Check the calibration on a recording that was not used for the solve.
MVIS has no command for this check. --independent-check holdout only records in the verdict that you ran one.

### Another tool

Run Kalibr or Basalt on the same recordings.
mvis.io.kalibr reads Kalibr’s camchains and results (Kalibr files).
The leaderboard shows MVIS, Kalibr and Basalt side by side.

### Digital twin

A digital twin replays a real recording’s motion, frame times and corner layout with known
parameters. Solving it measures bias against a truth no one gave the solver.
See Digital-twin check.

## Benchmark metrics

The leaderboard and each dataset’s eval page use these numbers.
Methodology explains how to read them.

Metric | Unit | What it is |
Median ± sd (n) | per parameter | Median and standard deviation of one tool’s estimate over the n recordings it solved |
Difference | per parameter | Difference of two tools’ medians; ◆ when it is larger than the larger of the two spreads |
Focal length, principal point | px | Camera intrinsics |
Lever arm | mm | Camera position in the base IMU frame, or auxiliary IMU position |
Rotation | rad | log(R) rotation vector of an extrinsic |
Stereo baseline | mm | Distance between two cameras |
td, t_ga | ms | Camera–IMU and gyro-to-accelerometer time offsets |
Solved | n of N | Recordings a tool solved |

The benchmark datasets have no ground truth.
A small spread shows repeatability, not accuracy, and a difference shows that two tools disagree,
not which one is right. Reprojection error is not compared across tools, because it measures fit.

## Reference values

Where a recording has published or factory values, the regression suite reports the
percentage difference to them (--gt). These values are compared, never used as a pass or fail gate.
They are kept with the regression suite.

## Regression suite

We run MVIS over real recordings and digital twins, and gate every change against stored baselines
with per-metric tolerances (focal length, distortion, extrinsics, time offsets, readout, reprojection).
